jobs.title: Sr. Manager Mergers and Acquisitions Integration
jobs.description:
Our Integration Management Office is the central hub that brings newly acquired businesses into Vertiv and turns our deal thesis into realized value. We are hiring a Senior Manager, Integration, to join the IMO and lead the integration of assigned acquisitions end to end, operating within our established integration governance, playbook, and toolset.

What you will own

Reporting to the Vice President, Global M&A Integration, you will serve as the integration lead for assigned the value-creation case from pre-close planning through Day 1 and the value-capture period that follows. You will drive the integration plan across functional workstreams, hold the program to the synergy and milestone commitments defined in diligence, and partner with acquired-company leadership to implement our integration playbook while protecting the talent, customers, and culture that made the business worth acquiring.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to

- Lead integrations end to end:  Own the integration roadmap for assigned deals, from diligence handoff and Day 1 readiness through the value-capture period, anchored to the value-creation thesis approved at deal approval.

- Run the integration within the IMO model:  Operate inside the IMO established governance, charters, tools, and templates; manage cross-functional workstreams across Finance, HR, IT, Operations, Commercial, Legal, and Supply Chain; and keep steering committees informed with a disciplined reporting cadence.

- Deliver measurable value capture:  Translate the deal model into tracked synergy and improvement commitments across safety, quality, delivery, and cost; establish the metrics, dashboards, and review rhythm that hold the integration accountable to the case.

- Deploy operational efficiency and integration playbook into acquired businesses:  Partner with acquired leadership to introduce lean and Lean Six Sigma processes, Value Stream Mapping, daily management, and policy deployment, establishing visual management so teams have immediate feedback on performance.

- Lead through influence:  Build trust quickly across newly acquired leadership teams, corporate functions, and IMO workstream leads, driving alignment without direct reporting authority.

- Protect what we acquired:  Steward culture, key talent, and customer relationships through the transition, recognizing that retaining the acquired team strengths is as critical to the thesis as capturing synergies.

- Strengthen the IMO playbook:  Capture lessons learned, refine integration tools and templates, and contribute to raising the consistency, maturity, and repeatability of integration across the Vertiv deal pipeline.

The essential requirements of the job include

- Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, finance, or a related field; MBA preferred.

- Eight or more years of progressive experience in M&A integration, corporate development, operations, program management, or management consulting, including direct experience leading or co-leading post-merger and post-acquisition integration.

- Demonstrated success delivering complex, cross-functional programs on time and on budget while leading through influence in a matrixed, global organization.

- Strong financial and analytical fluency, able to connect an integration plan to a deal model, synergy targets, and P&L outcomes.

- Working knowledge of lean and continuous-improvement methodologies such as Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, or an equivalent operating system.

- Excellent communication and change-leadership skills, credible with both frontline teams and senior executives.

- Willingness to travel 40 to 60 percent, including internationally.

It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in

- Operating within an established IMO or enterprise PMO across multiple, concurrent integrations.

- Critical infrastructure, power, thermal or cooling, electrical equipment, industrial technology, or data center end markets.

- Carve-out, cross-border, or bolt-on integration at scale across multiple acquisitions.

- A formal operating-system or continuous improvement practitioner or certification background, for example a Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent.

The successful candidate will embrace Vertiv’s Core Principles & Behaviors to help execute our Strategic Priorities.

OUR CORE PRINCIPLES :   Safety.  Integrity.  Respect.  Teamwork.  Inclusion.

OUR STRATEGIC PRIORITIES

•  High-Performance Culture

Customer Focus Operational Excellence

•  Innovation

•  Financial Strength

VERTIV BEHAVIORS

- Own it

- Act with urgency

- Foster a customer-first mindset

- Think big and execute

- Lead by example

- Drive continuous improvement

- Learn and seek out development

- Promote transparent & open communication

About Vertiv

Vertiv brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to enable its customers’ vital applications to run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs.  Vertiv solves the most important challenges facing today’s data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities with a portfolio of power, cooling and IT infrastructure solutions and services that extend from the cloud to the edge of the network. Headquartered in Westerville, Ohio, USA, Vertiv employs around 34,000 people and does business in more than 130 countries. Visit Vertiv.com to learn more.

jobs.title: Electrical Safety Program Manager
jobs.description:
Electrical Safety Program Manager:

This role is external facing, involving the development of site-based Electrical Safety Plans for customers.  Responsible for developing site based electrical safety programs, in addition to support, consultation, and implementation for external customers.  Provide support and direction for aspects of safety and environmental affairs. Responsible for consultation on corporate safety initiatives to minimize the number and reduce the severity of accidents and injuries while maintaining the efficiency of the jobsite and the well-being of employees. Drive global, regional, and multi-site safety program strategies across manufacturing, facilities, corporate offices, and client environments. Build prevention-focused safety cultures, sustain ISO certiﬁcations, reduce enterprise risk, and align EHS governance with business growth, sustainability, and customer expectations.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Define Safety Program elements and enterprise metrics for external customers.

- Develop electrical safety strategy and execution across multi-country business units, ensuring alignment with enterprise objectives, regulatory requirements, and ISO 14001 standards.

- Serve as senior advisor to external business and site leadership, partnering on capital projects, regulatory compliance initiatives, water recycling, pressure testing processes, and specialized risk-based training.

- Act as primary liaison with client leadership, legal, security, and facilities teams, aligning safety, emergency preparedness, ergonomics, and regulatory compliance with business and brand risk expectation.

- Provide customer site consultation for safety issues and or problems.

- Facilitation and involvement in Safety Committees.

- Review and assist with development of necessary plans, procedures and strategies implementation and ensures their consistency and adequacy.

- Interface with all levels of the organization

- Have strong working knowledge of Electrical Safety and NFPA 70, NFPA 70E and NFPA 70B.

- Conducts safety audits and hazard assessments when appropriate in conjunction with applicable safety programs and/or regulations.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Qualifications:  (education, experience level, knowledge, skills, designations/certifications).

- Bachelor’s degree desired, preferably in Electrical, Occupational Health and Safety or Safety Science.

- 5 to 10 years of experience in Electrical work (low and medium voltage) and/or Construction

- Strong organizational and research skills.

- Strong analytical skills.

- Excellent oral and written communication skills.

- Have excellent computer skills, MS Word, MS PowerPoint and MS Excel.

- Strong customer service skills.

- Broad knowledge of environmental, health, safety, NFPA 70E, Electrical and DOT regulatory compliance requirements.

- Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with all levels of management and staff.

- Demonstrated interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to work with necessary levels of management in integrating safe and healthy behaviors in day-day operations.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience supporting union labor environments.

- Experience working in data center or mission-critical construction environments.

- Experience supporting large-scale infrastructure or industrial construction projects.

- OSHA 30-Hour Construction Certification.

- STS-C (Safety Trained Supervisor – Construction) or CHST (Construction Health and Safety Technician) certification required within 90 days of hire.

- Additional professional certifications such as CSP (Certified Safety Professional) or related credentials.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications including Outlook, Word, and Excel.

Physical & Environmental Demands

- Ability to walk and stand for extended periods on active construction sites.

- Ability to work in both indoor and outdoor environments.

- Ability to safely navigate construction environments including uneven surfaces and elevated work areas.

Travel

- 30-50%

Courses and Qualiﬁcations

- OSHA 30-Hour General Industry

- OSHA 510 Construction

- Associate Safety Professional (ASP)

- Certiﬁed Safety Professional (CSP)

jobs.title: Strategic Planning Specialist
jobs.description:
Role Overview

In this role, you will be part of the Greater China President’s Office, serving as a strategy planner for the GC leadership team.

The position is responsible for driving market intelligence, strategic planning, and M&A analysis, including market modeling, growth opportunity assessment, target evaluation, and strategic investment support.

The role works closely with BU leaders, Finance, Strategy, and Global teams to provide data-driven insights and recommendations that support executive decision-making, business growth, and long-term value creation.

Key Responsibilities

- Develop and maintain GC market models and market intelligence frameworks to support strategic planning, business growth, and investment decisions.

- Analyze market opportunities, competitive dynamics, growth drivers, industry trends, emerging technologies across China and outbound business segments, generating actionable insights to support executive decision-making

- Support VPs in preparing Global& Regional QBRs, MBRs, management presentations, and external-facing materials through business analysis and strategic insights.

- Drive cross-functional alignment on market assumptions, demand outlooks, and business priorities across regional and global stakeholders.

- Support mergers & acquisitions assessments, strategic initiatives, and special projects through market analysis, due diligence coordination, and executive-level reporting.

- Prepare meeting minutes, track action items, and drive follow-through to ensure timely execution of key business decisions.  Support ad-hoc strategic initiatives and special projects assigned by VPs and the GC President’s Office.

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree or above in Business, Finance, Economics, Engineering, or related fields.

- 2–5 years of experience in strategy, consulting, finance, investment, or business analysis roles. Experience with M&A will be a plus.

- Strong analytical and structured thinking capability, with good communication and coordination skills; able to work with multiple functions and senior stakeholders.

- Fluent English (written and spoken) for working with Global teams.

- Proactive, self-driven, and able to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment with a strong ownership mindset.

- Strong analytical, data interpretation, and critical thinking skills, with the ability to leverage AI tools to generate actionable insights and support strategic planning and decision-making.

The Senior Manager, M&A plays a critical role in executing Vertiv’s inorganic growth strategy by leading complex transaction activities end ‑ to ‑ end, including opportunity evaluation, due diligence, and deal execution. This role operates at both an operational and strategic level—driving deal strategy, influencing cross-functional stakeholders, and ensuring successful execution of high-impact transactions aligned with business objectives.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Strategic Opportunity Evaluation

- Lead development of investment theses for acquisitions, divestitures, and partnerships aligned to business strategy

- Own complex valuation analyses (DCF, comparables, scenario modeling) and assess strategic fit, risks, and value creation opportunities

- Partner with senior business leaders to shape financial forecasts, synergy assumptions, and deal rationale

- Present recommendations and insights to senior leadership, influencing decision-making on transaction priorities

Transaction Leadership & Execution

- Lead cross-functional due diligence efforts, coordinating internal stakeholders and external advisors across multiple workstreams

- Direct financial diligence, identifying key risks, validating assumptions, and refining valuation models

- Drive issue identification, risk mitigation strategies, and integration considerations during deal execution

- Support negotiation strategy with fact-based insights and financial analytics to optimize deal outcomes

Program & Stakeholder Management

- Manage multiple concurrent transactions, ensuring alignment on priorities, timelines, and deliverables

- Influence senior stakeholders across Finance, Strategy, Legal, and Business Units to drive decisions and resolve issues

- Establish governance, reporting cadence, and executive updates for active deals

- Mentor and guide junior team members and analysts supporting transaction work

Integration & Value Realization

- Partner with integration teams to ensure continuity from diligence to execution of synergy capture plans

- Track and evaluate post-close performance against deal assumptions and value creation targets

- Identify lessons learned to inform future transaction strategy

KEY CAPABILITIES

- Advanced Financial & Strategic Acumen: Ability to translate complex analyses into clear business insights and recommendations

- Enterprise Influence: Proven ability to influence stakeholders across functions and seniority levels

- Leadership & Team Development: Experience leading or mentoring team members on complex workstreams

- Decision-Making in Ambiguity: Navigates moderately complex, high-impact decisions with incomplete information

- Execution Excellence: Drives multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously with strong project governance

QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business or related field

- 10+ years of relevant experience in corporate development, investment banking, private equity, or consulting

- Demonstrated experience leading M&A transactions or major workstreams end-to-end

- Strong financial modeling and valuation expertise

Preferred:

- MBA or advanced degree

- Experience in industrial manufacturing, critical infrastructure, or related sectors

- Exposure to global / cross-border transactions

Function/Department:  Strategy Office / Global Services

Reports to: Senior Director Service Strategy and Portfolio

Location:  Westerville

Vertiv, a $5.6B global organization with nearly 20,000 employees, designs, builds and services critical infrastructure that enables vital applications for data centers, communication networks, and commercial and industrial facilities.  We support today’s growing mobile and cloud computing markets with a portfolio of power, thermal and infrastructure management solutions.

Job Summary

The  Service Strategic Planner , reporting to the Senior Director Service Strategy and Portfolio, is responsible for maintaining, governing, and continuously improving the global service planning environment. This role ensures alignment between Corporate strategic directives and Global Business Unit (GBU) strategies, translating them into structured service roadmaps, portfolio priorities, and executable planning frameworks.

The position acts as the central coordination point for global service planning deliverables, ensuring visibility, consistency, prioritization, and governance across regions and business units. The role requires strong strategic thinking, structured planning capability, and the ability to operate across a complex, matrixed organization.

Responsibilities :

- Translate Corporate strategy into actionable service planning frameworks.

- Standardize planning templates, KPIs, and deliverable expectations across GBU and Regions.

- Ensure consistency, accuracy, and alignment of inputs for strategic corporate reviews and executive reporting.

- Support investment prioritization based on strategic impact, ROI, and resource capacity.

- Manage Global Service interlocks meetings cadence in the overall company executive calendar.

- Be the focal point and drive pro-active project cadence and “drumbeat” with a diverse set of stakeholders to ensure timely and successful outcomes.

- Coordinate preparation of corporate-required planning deliverables (strategy reviews, growth plans, transformation updates).

- Develop executive-level presentations and dashboards.

- Provide structured insights and scenario analysis to senior leadership.

- Track performance against strategic targets.

- Ensure transparency and communication across matrix stakeholders

- Support teams and business leaders in structuring business cases, customer segmentation, competitive analysis, value-based pricing, economic benchmarking, and service strategic performance analyses across business segments.

- Structure customer and market-segmentation, developing and working with market models, deriving insight from internal and external data sources.

Recommendations and Execution :

- Ability to self-manage multiple projects and work streams in a dynamic international environment.

- Work collaboratively and support multi-departmental efforts and projects.

- Communicate effectively across the organization and be flexible in managing diverse tasks and assignments.

Requirements :

- Minimum 5+ years of experience as internal strategic planning or business consulting function.

- Degree in business administration, Marketing, Finance, or related field; MBA preferred.

- Program management experience

- Core Competencies:

- Proven experience supporting investment prioritization and business case evaluation, with strong capabilities in long-range planning and scenario modeling.

- Strong organizational and coordination capability across global stakeholders.

- Demonstrated ability to build trusted executive relationships and communicate effectively across diverse international cultures.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Strategy & Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Manufacturing Strategy & Operations Lead

We are seeking a highly skilled candidate with deep expertise in manufacturing operations, industrial engineering, and capacity planning. This individual will support the development and execution of global manufacturing strategies — including footprint optimization and capital investment planning — to ensure scalable, cost-effective operations that align with long-term business growth at an expanding F500 company.

The ideal candidate brings hands-on manufacturing leadership experience, a global mindset, cross-functional collaboration skills, and proven experience working across multiple product lines, facilities, and regions.

Responsibilities:

Manufacturing Strategy & Global Footprint Optimization

- Evaluate and recommend manufacturing footprint strategies considering factors such as cost, geopolitical risk, technology enablement, supply chain resiliency, and customer proximity.

- Identify demand signals, determine capacity constraints, and drive cross-functional collaboration to solve for any capacity gaps.

- Support make-vs-buy and vertical integration analyses aligned with product and process needs.

Capacity Planning & CAPEX Management

- Conduct in-depth capacity modeling, scenario planning, and throughput analysis for multiple product lines.

- Lead capital expenditure planning and justification for manufacturing investments, equipment, and facility expansions.

- Identify and implement solutions to optimize plant loading, equipment utilization, and capital deployment.

- Partner with regional and plant teams to ensure alignment with growth forecasts and demand variability.

Scalability & Industrial Engineering

- Apply industrial engineering principles to drive efficiency, throughput, and continuous improvement across manufacturing sites.

- Conduct manufacturing research to evaluate emerging technologies, processes, and production methodologies.

- Promote scalable manufacturing processes, modular BoP strategies, and digital factory principles.

- Support new product introduction by integrating design for manufacturability principles and capacity readiness into early planning.

Cross-Functional & Global Collaboration

- Collaborate with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Finance to ensure cross-functional alignment on strategic manufacturing decisions.

- Own stakeholder management to the executive level, presenting to senior leadership on a regular basis.

- Support product transfers and ramp-ups across regions, ensuring minimal disruption and operational continuity.

Data-Driven Decision Making

- Leverage manufacturing and business intelligence data (e.g., MES, ERP, capacity tools) to drive strategic planning.

- Develop and maintain models for manufacturing cost, utilization, and capacity scenario analysis.

A Strong Candidate Will Bring:

- Bachelor's Degree in Industrial Engineering/Technology, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics, or equivalent experience

- 7–10 years of experience in manufacturing operations, industrial engineering, or plant leadership

- Knowledge of global supply chain dynamics, geopolitical influences, and total landed cost analysis

- Strong communication, leadership, and project management skills; able to influence at all levels

- Lean Six Sigma or continuous improvement background

- Experience managing manufacturing footprint requirements and facility planning

- Strong CAPEX planning and justification experience

- Strong analytical skills, including financial modeling and use of simulation or capacity planning software (e.g., Simio or equivalent)

- Experience with digital manufacturing tools (e.g., MES, digital twins) is a plus.

- Prior experience in plant management, production management, or multi-shift operations leadership preferred

TRAVEL REQUIREMENT : 10%

jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Manager
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The VOS Manager at the manufacturing site serves as the primary driver of the Vertiv Operating System (VOS), accountable for translating global standards into daily operational excellence and sustained cultural adoption. This role leads the deployment, governance, and continuous improvement of VOS across all functions, ensuring full alignment with Strategy Deployment, Tier Accountability, and Order-to-Fulfillment (OTF) processes. Acting as a strategic partner to the Site Leader, the VOS Manager embeds disciplined execution through Leader Standard Work, problem-solving (RCA), and escalation routines, while building organizational capability through structured training, coaching, and certification. The VOS Manager also serves as the site’s Lean subject matter expert (SME) and a fundamental point of reference, providing hands-on coaching and guidance to leaders and teams to ensure consistent understanding and effective implementation of Lean principles and practices. The position is responsible for ensuring compliance with global standards, driving measurable performance improvements across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and inventory, and preparing the site for VOS Capability Assessments. Ultimately, the VOS Manager enables sustainable results by integrating systems, developing people, and reinforcing a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.

RESPONSIBILITIES

-
VOS Deployment & Governance

-
Lead end-to-end deployment of the Vertiv Operating System (VOS) across all site functions, ensuring full adherence to global standards and controlled documentation.

-
Translate VOS requirements into practical, site-level execution plans with clear milestones, ownership, and measurable outcomes.

-
Maintain strict compliance with VOS global templates, standards, and “Rules of Engagement,” ensuring no unauthorized deviations.

-
Act as the site’s subject matter expert (SME) for all 17 VOS elements, ensuring balanced maturity and integration across the system.

-
Tier Accountability & Daily Management System

-
Design, implement, and sustain Tier 1–Tier 3 (and Tier 4 where applicable) accountability structures aligned with global standards.

-
Ensure 100% compliance on Tier board content, KPIs, and standard meeting agendas across all levels.

-
Drive disciplined execution of daily operating cadence, ensuring real-time visibility, escalation, and follow-up of issues.

-
Audit Tier meetings regularly to ensure quality of discussions, data accuracy, and leadership engagement.

-
Performance Management & KPI Governance

-
Own the deployment and sustainment of site-level KPI frameworks aligned with global scorecards and MOR requirements.

-
Ensure KPIs are clearly defined, cascaded, and actively managed through Tier meetings and leadership routines.

-
Lead data integrity and validation processes to ensure accuracy and reliability of reported performance.

-
Support site leadership in performance reviews, identifying gaps, trends, and required corrective actions.

-
Problem Solving, RCA & Escalation

-
Embed structured problem-solving methodologies (RCA, 5 Whys, 8D) into daily operations, ensuring they are not treated as standalone activities.

-
Ensure all significant deviations are properly escalated through defined pathways with clear ownership and timing.

-
Drive closure discipline: problem identification → root cause → corrective action → standardization → sustainment.

-
Coach leaders and teams on effective problem-solving techniques and escalation behaviors.

-
Capability Building & Training

-
Develop and execute a structured VOS capability-building roadmap for all levels of the organization.

-
Ensure compliance with training requirements, including role-based training, certification, and traceability of training records.

-
Coach site leadership (from frontline supervisors to site manager) on VOS principles, behaviors, and expectations.

-
Build internal capability through mentoring, practical application, and reinforcement of standard work.

-
Leader Standard Work (LSW)

-
Define, implement, and sustain Leader Standard Work across all leadership levels.

-
Ensure LSW is consistently executed, audited, and continuously improved.

-
Align LSW with Tier Accountability, KPI reviews, Gemba walks, and escalation routines.

-
Reinforce leadership discipline and accountability through structured routines.

-
Continuous Improvement & Lean Deployment

-
Drive continuous improvement initiatives aligned with VOS elements, including 5S+1, standard work, material flow, TPM, and process optimization.

-
Lead Kaizen events and structured improvement cycles focused on eliminating waste and improving flow.

-
Ensure improvements are standardized, documented, and sustained over time.

-
Promote a culture of proactive problem identification and continuous improvement across all functions.

-
OTF (Order-to-Fulfillment) Integration

-
Ensure full integration of VOS with OTF processes, including planning, scheduling, production execution, and logistics.

-
Support deployment of L2/L3 OTF processes and ensure alignment with Tier Accountability and KPI frameworks.

-
Drive cross-functional coordination to meet customer commitments (SSD) and improve delivery performance.

-
Monitor OTF-related KPIs and ensure issues are escalated and resolved effectively.

-
Audit Readiness & Capability Assessment

-
Lead preparation for VOS Capability Assessments (Rookie, Challenger, and beyond), ensuring site readiness across all elements.

-
Conduct internal pre-assessments and gap analyses to identify risks and required corrective actions.

-
Coordinate audit activities, including documentation, evidence preparation, and stakeholder alignment.

-
Ensure timely closure of audit findings with robust corrective actions.

-
Cross-Functional Alignment

-
Drive alignment across all site functions (Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, EHS, Engineering, HR) to ensure integrated VOS execution.

-
Facilitate collaboration between departments to eliminate silos and improve end-to-end process performance.

-
Ensure VOS principles are embedded beyond manufacturing, supporting enterprise-wide adoption where applicable.

-
Standardization & Documentation Control

-
Ensure all VOS-related documentation is current, controlled, and aligned with global standards.

-
Work closely with global document control to implement updates and revisions effectively.

-
Prevent local deviations by reinforcing the importance of a single source of truth.

-

jobs.description:
Position Summary

Vertiv is seeking a Director, Inventory Strategy and Planning to support the Americas region. This role will lead the development and execution of inventory strategies that ensure material availability in support of production requirements while optimizing inventory investment and trade working capital performance. Responsibilities

- Present inventory performance, risks, opportunities, and mitigation plans to executive leadership teams.

- Drive the inventory portion of the sales, inventory, and operations planning (SIOP).

- Own and execute the monthly inventory forecast process

- Evaluate forecast accuracy and performance, identifying root causes of variation and systemic drivers

- Drive process improvements and establish tools to improve the quality and reliability of inventory forecasts.

- Develop strategies to optimize inventory levels

- Establish inventory targets for each factory and create supporting plans to achieve the targets.

jobs.title: Financial Planning and Analysis Specialist
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

-
The Senior Analyst, FP&A is a key member of the Business Finance Organization responsible for delivering end-to-end financial planning and forecasting process and serves as the primary finance business partners to the business leaders. This role independently owns workstreams across forecasting, working capital management, variance analysis, and financial modelling — translating complex data into actionable insights that drive strategic and operational decisions aligned to global guidance and regional execution.

RESPONSIBILITIES

End-to-End FP&A Process Ownership (Primary)

- Own and drive the full forecasting cycle for assigned Product Lines / BUs — from data gathering through analysis, alignment with business partners, submission, reconciliation, and sign-off

- Build and maintain bottom-up and top-down forecast models for Orders, Sales, and Margin by product line, incorporating pipeline, backlog, pricing actions, mix assumptions and other key drivers

- Drive forecast accuracy through continuous methodology improvement, tracking, and root-cause analysis

- Own the forecast walk process — clearly articulating movements between forecast with drivers and mitigation plans/actions

- Coordinate forecast inputs across global and regional cross functional teams, including commercial, supply chain, operations and product management to ensure alignment and completeness

- Manage forecast consolidation and reconciliation across systems, ensuring data integrity from source to submission

- Own the working capital monthly forecasting process, understand and validate inputs, monitor and manage TWC metrics for a review.

- Prepare and present the monthly TWC Executive Overview including step charts showing TWC evolution (quarterly trend from actuals through forecast periods)

Business Partnering with Product Line / BU P&L Owners (Primary)

- Serve as the dedicated finance partner to Product Line / BU P&L leaders — proactively providing financial insights on P&L performance

- Partner independently with the Product Offering Organization to understand product roadmaps, pricing strategies, new product development introductions (NPDI), and their financial implications

- Collaborate with Global BU Finance to align regional forecasts with global targets, reconcile variances, and ensure consistent assumptions across geographies

- Provide P&L owners with monthly/quarterly performance packs including variance analysis (Actual vs. Target vs. Prior Forecast), trend commentary, and forward-looking risk/opportunity assessments

- Challenge and validate assumptions to ensure forecast credibility

- Support P&L owners in preparing for global reviews — providing data, talking points, and bridge analyses

- Track and analyze Orders performance by product line — identifying trends, risks, and upside opportunities

- Monitor pipeline coverage ratios and pipeline conversion rates to inform forecast assumptions, quantify pipeline gaps and work with commercial teams to identify actions to close shortfalls

- Analyze book-to-bill ratios and order intake patterns to inform forward-looking Sales and Margin projections

- Deliver detailed sales and margins analysis by product line, decomposing performance into volume, price, mix, and cost drivers

- Perform bridge/walk analyses to clearly show key drivers and impacts to drive urgency and action

- Analyze product mix shifts and their margin implications — flagging structural trends that require management attention

- Conduct structured variance analysis with commentary and prepare executive-ready reports for leadership reviews

Process Improvement & Systems

- Identify and drive process improvements — reducing month-end cycle time, improving data quality, and enhancing automation

- Support system and tool enhancements to improve forecasting efficiency and reporting quality

- Develop standardized templates and automate dashboards for Product Line / BU performance tracking

- Direct interface in dispute resolution process to ensure timely problem resolution.  As required work with functional owners on problem solution and escalate to upper management when required.

- Supports the cross-functional initiatives, independently serve as trust finance business partner to broader organization.

- Assist management in forecasting and reporting in accordance with reporting requirements.

- Support ad hoc duties and lead special projects as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Job Qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business or related field

-
4-8 years of progressive FP&A or Business Finance experience in a multinational environment

Preferred Qualifications:

- Strong proficiency in financial modeling — particularly Orders/Sales/Margin forecasting and variance analysis

- Demonstrated experience as a finance business partner to P&L leaders

- Advanced Excel skills; experience with ERP systems (e.g., Oracle, HFM, Essbase, EPM)

- Ability to work independently across matrix organizations (regional teams, global functions, product organizations)

- ERP Systems experience, preferably Oracle.

- Professional certification (CPA, CMA, ACCA, or equivalent)

- Experience with BI/analytics tools (Power BI)

- Regional/multi-country finance experience (Asia-Pacific preferred)

EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATIONS

- Bachelor’s degree in business or related field

-
MBA desirable but not required

jobs.title: Manager Operations Management - Final Assembly
jobs.description:
As the Operations Manager you will directly manage the supervisors of the APU (autonomous production unit) site and have overall responsibility for the full scope of assembly operations. The Operations Manager directs and coordinates functions for the product line including manufacturing, supply chain, on time delivery quality, and operational excellence. You will plan, coordinate, supervise and motivate the activities of all assigned employees as well as the utilization of employees assigned to peer lines to meet or exceed safety, quality, delivery, cost, and efficiency goals and supporting plant wide initiatives.

What You’ll Be Doing

- Manage multiple production supervisors across a 24/7 manufacturing operation.

- Lead production and operations to troubleshoot and improve areas related to:

- Machine downtime.

- Production schedules.

- Product quality.

- On time delivery.

- Make operational decisions and engage technical staff as needed for support.

- Determine manpower requirements to meet production schedules.

- Participate in employment and staffing decisions/performance management decisions.

- Promote regular communication and motivation to achieve production goals.

- Implement elements of the organizational development (OD) plan, including:

- Process control strategy.

- Organizational strategy.

Safety & Compliance

- Lead and promote the Plant Safety Process across the Value Stream.

- Maintain strong operating discipline and awareness around plant safety policies.

- Drive safety-focused Lean events related to process effectiveness and cost reduction.

- Promote excellence in housekeeping, 5S and workplace organization.

Continuous Improvement & Lean Manufacturing

- Address and remove waste from the operation.

- Develop processes and systems for continuous improvement.

- Maintain quality performance through systems management and Lean principles.

- Support and participate in Lean Manufacturing initiatives.

- Recommend and manage Lean events focused on:

- Safety.

- Cycle time reduction.

- Cost reduction.

- Establish Lean events to improve housekeeping and reduce operational effort/cost.

Leadership, Employee Relations & Development

- Partner with HR to develop and coach supervisors and other staff members

- Lead, coach, and support supervisors in policy interpretation, labor relations, and operational performance

- Interview and help select qualified employees

- Ensure onboarding, departmental induction, and job training are completed effectively

- Promote positive employee relations and maintain strong communication with employees

- Provide ongoing performance assessment and feedback for supervisors and technical staff

- Support employee involvement through:

- Frequent employee meetings

- Problem-solving activities

- Recognition programs

- Information sharing

- Delegation of responsibility

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Work closely with the Plant Leadership Team and other Operations managers

- Communicate business unit performance, operational issues, and improvement activities

- Maintain strong customer awareness and focus on delivering product that meets customer requirements

What Will Make You Successful

- Strong safety leadership and commitment to plant safety culture

- Ability to lead operations in a fast-paced manufacturing environment

- Strong organizational and operational decision-making skills

- Proven ability to organize, implement, and sustain change initiatives

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

- Ability to coach, mentor, and develop supervisors and employees

- Strong employee relations and conflict resolution capabilities

- Ability to balance production, maintenance, quality, and operational priorities

- Strong cross-functional collaboration and leadership skills

- Ability to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence

- Strong customer-focused mindset

- Ability to manage performance and accountability across a 24/7 operation

What Makes You Stand Out

- Bachelor’s degree in a technical field

- 3+ years of supervisory or manufacturing leadership experience

- Experience working in a manufacturing environment

- Knowledge of:

- Lean Manufacturing

- Six Sigma methodologies

- Organizational development

- Human resources practices

- Experience leading Lean events and continuous improvement initiatives

- Strong systems management and process improvement background

Vertiv is hiring a Program Manager in Westerville, OH to join our execution team, this role will provide value to our customers by overseeing strategic initiatives across one or more global strategic accounts. This role will be involved from quoting phase through the operational phase of all customer sites as well as work on initiatives within Vertiv that aid the account. - Oversee deployment of field change notice (FCN) and factory direct service (FDS).

- Ensure all change orders are entered properly in CPQ and are booked in EBS.

- Other duties as assigned by manager.

- 5+ years of relative industry experience, preferably in manufacturing or supply chain environment

- Prior experience indirectly influencing project teams

• Hands-on experience in the application of Lean/Six Sigma methods and way of thinking.

• Strong leadership, organizational, project management and inter-personal skills.

• Excellent oral and written communication skills in local language and English.

• Strong analytical skills, including the use of statistical modeling techniques, root cause analysis and other tools and methods typically deployed to drive operational improvements.

• Ability to influence and lead in a matrix organization to drive accountably and execution of VOS mindset and activities.

• Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent of 5 plus years’ experience.

- Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously

- Understanding service P&L

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills for effective stakeholder management

- Analytical and problem-solving capabilities with a data-driven approach

- Proficiency in ERP/inventory management systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle)

- Strong understanding of warranty processes and service level agreements (SLAs)

- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment

- Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word)

- Fluent in Bahasa Indonesia and English (written and spoken)

- PMP or equivalent project management certification

- Experience with Vertiv or similar OEM products and services

- Knowledge of the Indonesia market and channel distribution landscape

jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Coordinator - Manufacturing Support
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Continuous Improvement Coordinator supports daily Vertiv Operating System (VOS) activities across two manufacturing sites through hands‑on coordination, auditing, and visual management support. This is a highly floor‑based role , spending the majority of time working directly with production teams to ensure CI processes are followed consistently and documentation stays accurate and up to date.

This position is well‑suited for someone with manufacturing floor experience who enjoys structured work, recurring audits, and partnering with employees at all levels. The role supports a small CI team and focuses on consistent execution of established CI processes in a fast‑paced manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities

- Conduct weekly  5S audits , track corrective actions, and follow up on overdue items.

- Perform regular  Leader Standard Work (LSW) audits and maintain current user rosters.

- Track  Tier meeting execution and ensure Tier boards remain complete and current (training matrices, visuals, metrics).

- Maintain  visual management boards , including printing materials, updating information, and managing labels, magnets, and signage.

- Support CI workshops and meetings by preparing pre‑work packets, tracking attendance, documenting action items, and assisting with logistics.

- Gather quotes and submit CI‑related purchase requests through  iProcurement .

- Maintain a centralized library for CI documents, templates, and standard tools.

- Pull reports from the  CI Idea System and prepare basic summaries.

- Take photos, notes, and document findings from 5S walks, audits, and CI activities.

- Partner closely with production, quality, and leadership teams to support daily CI expectations.

Qualifications

Required:

- 1–3 years of experience in a  manufacturing or industrial environment , with regular time spent on the production floor.

- Strong working knowledge of  Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint .

- Comfortable communicating with hourly employees, supervisors, and leadership.

- Organized, detail‑oriented, and able to manage recurring tasks and audits with consistency.

- Willingness to stay engaged on the production floor for the majority of the workday.

- Able to adapt to changing priorities while maintaining routine deliverables.

- Ability to travel between  two local manufacturing sites .

Preferred:

- Experience supporting or participating in  5S, Lean, LSW, Tier boards, audits, or visual management .

- Background in roles such as production support, audit coordination, quality support, safety coordination, or CI support.

- Bilingual (English/Spanish).

Physical & Environmental Requirements

- Frequent walking on the production floor; occasional standing during audits or meetings.

- Must follow required  PPE and safety protocols .

- Work performed primarily in an active manufacturing environment with limited desk time.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Procurement Ops & Supply Chain Transformation
jobs.description:
Vertiv is seeking a strategic, results-driven leader to transform Procurement Operations across the Americas. As the Senior Manager, Procurement Operations & Supply Chain Transformation, you will lead operational excellence initiatives that improve procurement performance, strengthen supplier partnerships, optimize business processes, and drive scalable growth.

Success in this role requires a strong procurement and supply chain leader who leverages Digital Solutions—including automation, analytics, AI-enabled capabilities, enterprise systems, and data-driven insights—to modernize operations, improve visibility, accelerate decision making, and deliver measurable business results. Technology is not the objective; it is the catalyst that enables procurement transformation.

Working cross-functionally with Category Management, Supplier Management, Operations, Manufacturing, Engineering, Finance, IT, Digital Solutions, and Global Supply Chain teams, you'll help shape the future of procurement while developing a high-performing team focused on innovation, continuous improvement, and customer value.

What You'll Do

- Lead and develop the Americas Procurement Operations team, establishing strategic priorities, building organizational capability, and fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

- Drive operational excellence across procurement, purchasing, sourcing execution, and supplier operations.

- Standardize and optimize procurement processes by leveraging digital workflows, automation, and system-driven controls to improve efficiency, compliance, consistency, and scalability.

- Lead business transformation initiatives that streamline workflows, reduce cycle times, eliminate manual processes, and improve operational performance through process digitization and data-driven decision making.

- Partner with Category Management, Supplier Management, Operations, Engineering, Manufacturing, Finance, IT, and Digital Solutions to improve supplier performance, inventory optimization, material availability, supply continuity, and cost performance.

- Leverage Power BI, enterprise reporting, advanced analytics, and real-time dashboards to monitor KPIs, identify opportunities, improve visibility, and enable faster business decisions.

- Champion the adoption of procurement technologies, automation, and digital capabilities that improve productivity, compliance, user experience, and organizational effectiveness.

- Utilize predictive analytics, planning tools, and operational insights to improve procurement planning and support informed business decisions.

- Lead change management initiatives that accelerate adoption of new processes, systems, and digital solutions across the organization.

- Serve as a trusted business partner, driving collaboration across functions to deliver measurable operational and business outcomes.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field.

- 7+ years of progressive leadership experience in Procurement, Supply Chain, Strategic Sourcing, Procurement Operations, or Operations.

- 3+ years of experience leading, coaching, and developing high-performing teams.

- Strong knowledge of procurement operations, supplier management, inventory planning, sourcing, and supply chain best practices.

- Demonstrated success leading cross-functional operational excellence, process improvement, or procurement transformation initiatives.

- Experience leveraging ERP platforms (Oracle, SAP, or similar), procurement technologies, and digital tools to improve business performance.

- Experience using Power BI, dashboards, analytics, and reporting to drive operational visibility and data-driven decision making.

- Strong understanding of workflow automation, business process optimization, and digital enablement within procurement or supply chain operations.

- Excellent leadership, communication, project management, and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred Qualifications

- MBA or Master's degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, or a related discipline.

- Experience within a manufacturing, industrial, or global operations environment.

- Experience with Oracle Cloud, Microsoft Power Platform, SharePoint, AI-enabled business tools, or similar enterprise technologies.

- Lean Six Sigma, CPSM, CSCP, APICS, or other relevant professional certifications.

Travel: Up to 10%.

Why Join Vertiv?

At Vertiv, you'll have the opportunity to lead meaningful transformation across a global procurement organization. You'll partner with experienced leaders, influence enterprise-wide initiatives, and help shape the future of procurement through operational excellence, innovation, and the strategic application of digital solutions. If you're passionate about building high-performing teams, modernizing business processes, and delivering measurable business impact, we'd love to hear from you.

The successful candidate will embrace Vertiv’s Core Principals & Behaviors to help execute our Strategic Priorities.

OUR CORE PRINCIPALS:   Safety.  Integrity. Respect.  Teamwork.  Diversity & Inclusion.

OUR STRATEGIC PRIORITIES

- Customer Focus

- Operational Excellence

- High-Performance Culture

- Innovation

- Financial Strength

OUR BEHAVIORS

- Own It

- Act With Urgency

- Foster a Customer-First Mindset

- Think Big and Execute

- Lead by Example

- Drive Continuous Improvement

- Learn and Seek Out Development

- Promote Transparent & Open Communication

At Vertiv, we’re on a mission to empower the people that will power the future. From a simple swipe to life-changing medicines, from push notifications to generative AI. We design, manufacture, and service the products and solutions that keep the world connected.  With $6.9 billion in revenue, a strong customer base and global reach spanning nearly 70 countries, we are uniquely positioned to deliver greater value to our customers and create new opportunities for our people.

If you are interested in applying or learning more about this role, please visit the company’s career page located on Vertiv.com/Careers

Work Authorization

No calls or agencies please. Vertiv will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. This is not a position for which sponsorship will be provided. Individuals with temporary visas such as E, F-1, H-1, H-2, L, B, J, or TN or who need sponsorship for work authorization now or in the future, are not eligible for hire.

Vertiv is seeking an experienced and collaborative Human Resources Business Partner to join our team in Anderson, SC, supporting the overnight shift.The schedule will be Monday - Thursday 3:00 pm to 1:00 am .

In this role, you will serve as a strategic partner to business leaders, providing guidance and support across all areas of human resources. The HRBP will balance business objectives with employee advocacy to drive organizational performance, employee engagement, and a high-performance culture.

This position requires strong employee relations expertise, sound judgment, problem-solving skills, conflict resolution capabilities, and the ability to coach leaders through complex workforce matters. The HRBP will partner closely with site and functional leadership to support talent development, workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, change management, and employee engagement initiatives. The successful candidate will promote Vertiv's values and behaviors while delivering practical HR solutions that support business goals and enhance the employee experience

Partner with manufacturing leadership to provide strategic HR guidance, employee relations support, and coaching that improves workforce effectiveness and business performance.

Lead complex employee relations investigations, conflict resolution efforts, and corrective action processes while ensuring consistent application of company policies and employment practices.

Drive onboarding and integration activities to ensure a positive, consistent experience for new employees and accelerate productivity and retention.

jobs.title: Sr. Portfolio Marketing Manager - Software
jobs.description:
The world depends on the data we power and cool™. Vertiv is a global leader in critical digital infrastructure for applications in data centers, communication networks, and commercial and industrial environments. The AI revolution is rewriting the rules of digital infrastructure, demanding solutions that move as one. Vertiv delivers end-to-end infrastructure where power, cooling, IT, and services work in unison - and, increasingly, where software is the layer that ties it all together. With our industry-leading technologies and global services network, we are fueling the revolution of the digital world, keeping technology ecosystems running efficiently and without interruption. Built for multiple compute generations ahead, Vertiv empowers customers to stay resilient, optimized, and future-ready. As a publicly traded, S&P 500 company (NYSE: VRT), Vertiv operates globally, serving customers in over 130 countries with $10.2 billion in sales.

Role Summary

AI is pushing data centers toward higher density, faster deployment, and far greater operational complexity - and software is the layer that makes all of it manageable. Controls, monitoring, and digital services are central to how customers evaluate, buy, and operate critical infrastructure today, and Vertiv is significantly expanding its investment in how that story is told to the market.

The Sr. Portfolio Marketing Manager – Software position is a high-visibility opportunity to build and scale Vertiv's software portfolio marketing strategy - shaping the narrative, go-to-market motion, and marketing systems for a rapidly growing part of the business. Software expertise lives across engineering and product teams. Your job is to unify that innovation into one coherent, category-defining story, working closely with a senior software leader who owns the broader software strategy, and with the technical leaders and teams behind it.

This is a senior, ownership-driven strategic role for someone who wants to build and scale rather than maintain an existing playbook. You'll partner with software engineering and product leadership, and collaborate closely with sales, brand, communications, and regional marketing teams globally to bring the software story to market.

What makes this role different:

- High-growth, high-visibility.  As a fast-growing and strategically important area within Vertiv, this role gives you the mandate to build a marketing strategy that matches its trajectory.

- One story, many teams.  Software talent and IP live across dedicated teams. You'll be the connective tissue that turns distributed technical work into a single, cohesive narrative.

- Outcomes over features.  Every narrative starts with what software unlocks for customers - visibility, uptime, faster response, lower risk, smarter decisions - with the technology following the outcome.

- Category leadership.  You'll help define how the market understands Vertiv's role in controls, monitoring, and digital services as AI reshapes the data center.

Responsibilities

- Own the software portfolio narrative for Vertiv including controls, monitoring, digital services, and related platforms while establishing a single, cohesive point of view across business units.

- Partner with the senior leadership, product leaders and software engineering to translate distributed technical innovation into unified positioning and messaging.

- Build and maintain the marketing infrastructure for software portfolio marketing: processes, launch frameworks, templates, and sales enablement systems.

- Develop and lead go-to-market strategy and launch plans for software products and platforms, including how software connects to and elevates Vertiv's power, thermal, and services offerings.

- Build detailed persona profiles for the software buying group distinct from traditional buyers.

- Own positioning and messaging for the software portfolio; serve as the marketing subject matter expert on software content across written, media, event, and sales channels.

- Design and deliver sales enablement materials and training that equip global and regional sales teams to sell controls, monitoring, and digital services with confidence.

- Track software, digital infrastructure, and monitoring/DCIM market trends and the competitive landscape to continually sharpen positioning.

- Present software portfolio strategy, plans, and results to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

- Collaborate across brand, communications, digital/web, demand generation, and business-unit marketing to align software initiatives with broader marketing objectives.

- Apply Vertiv Operating System discipline - best-practice sharing, continuous improvement, and management cadence with clear metrics and accountability - to a function that is still being defined.

Qualifications

- 12+ years in product marketing, product management, or technical marketing, with meaningful experience in enterprise software, or platform marketing.

- Experience building a marketing function, program, or go-to-market engine - comfortable defining the playbook rather than executing an existing one.

- Background in data center, IT, digital infrastructure, industrial software, or a related technology ecosystem; experience with controls, monitoring, DCIM, or energy/asset management software is a strong plus.

- Proven ability to translate deep technical capability into clear, outcome-driven narratives for both technical and business audiences.

- Track record of unifying input from multiple stakeholders or teams into one coherent strategy - this role requires influence without direct authority across business units.

- Experience partnering with senior technical and business leaders, including comfort presenting strategy and results to executive audiences.

- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders across geographies, with a strong bias toward action in ambiguous, still-forming environments.

- Strong data analysis skills, with the ability to tailor findings for audiences ranging from engineering to the C-suite.

- Excellent organizational skills, high attention to detail, and a builder's mindset.

Travel

10-15%

jobs.title: Product Line Project Manager, Global Procurement
jobs.description:
Job Description:

The Product Line Project Manager, Global Procurement is the single point of contact for Procurement on assigned projects (NPDI, ETO, SFA, VAVE, sustaining). This is an individual contributor role responsible for establishing a resilient, cost‑effective, and scalable supply chain for new products by driving early supplier engagement, sourcing strategy execution, and procurement readiness throughout the NPDI phase‑gate process.

Responsibilities:

Project Ownership and Cross-Functional Alignment

- Serve as the primary Procurement representative for assigned projects from early concept through production readiness.

- Ensure procurement deliverables are planned, tracked, and executed in alignment with NPDI phase-gate requirements.

- Represent Procurement at NPDI gate reviews, providing clear visibility into sourcing maturity, gaps, and mitigations.

- Track and report key metrics such as cost, lead time, supplier performance, and launch readiness.

- Partner closely with Engineering, Program Management, Commodity Management, Quality, and Operations teams to ensure sourcing strategies support overall project objectives.

- Act as the primary escalation point for procurement related risks impacting cost, schedule, or supply resilience.

Early Supplier Engagement and Sourcing Strategy

- Engage proactively with Engineering to understand component requirements early in the design process.

- Engage suppliers early to assess technical capability, capacity, cost drivers, and lead time expectations.

- Send early RFQs/RFPs ahead of design release and drive competitive bidding to achieve cost targets.

- Facilitate collaboration between Engineering and suppliers to improve design for manufacturability, cost efficiency, and supply flexibility.

- Establish strong supplier partnerships to drive innovation, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement.

- Ensure sourcing approaches align with established commodity strategies and preferred supplier frameworks.

Cost, Risk, and Supply Chain Readiness

- Support prototype, pilot, and pre-production builds, ensuring on-time availability of materials and services.

- Ensure sourcing aligns with NPDI resilience expectations (multi‑source, regional manufacturing, avoidance of single‑point failures).

- Use standardized BOM cost and risk tracking tools to maintain consistency and transparency.

- Promote reuse of existing, qualified components and architectures where feasible to improve cost, availability, and time‑to‑market.

- Drive sourcing maturity and readiness prior to product release to minimize disruption during ramp up and production.

Qualifications:

An ideal candidate will bring…

- Experience in Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, or Supply Chain, supporting new product or engineering driven programs.

- Experience working closely with Engineering teams during early product development.

- Strong communication skills with the ability to influence across functions without direct authority.

- Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a matrixed, cross functional environment.

- Experience supporting global supply chains and multiple manufacturing regions.

- Familiarity with phase-gate or structured product development processes.

Education:

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Mechanical, Industrial, Electrical, Electronic), Supply Chain Operations and/or Business is preferred.

Physical Requirements:

- No Special Physical Requirements

Environmental Demands:

- No Specific Environmental Demands

Travel Time Required:

- Ability to work overtime and travel (domestically and internationally) up to 15% is required.

- Ability to work as per Project priorities and take after hours calls as necessary.

- Commercial launch planning

- AI and digital tool opportunities to improve product management effectiveness

- Growth strategy development for existing and emerging product lines

- Research and analysis of industry trends impacting data center infrastructure

Qualifications

Required

- Currently enrolled in an MBA program with expected graduation within 12-24 months.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

- Excellent verbal, written, and presentation communication skills.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.

- Demonstrated ability to synthesize data into actionable business recommendations.

- Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred

- Undergraduate degree in engineering, business, computer science, or a related technical field.

- Prior experience in product management, strategy, consulting, engineering, operations, or technology industries.

- Interest in data center infrastructure, power systems, electrical equipment, industrial technology, or AI-related markets.

jobs.description:
Business Unit Job Summary:  A brief synopsis of the role for this set of work.   This summary can include details about products, regions, scope and other details unique to a GBU, department or position.

The primary function will be to plan and perform sales and marketing efforts for the Service Center.  This role is responsible for an area of geography which could include multiple service center locations.  This role is responsible for acting as a technical expert with the region to support complex job walks, bid responses and technical conversations with clients.  .  This activity will be done using all principles of good salesmanship, including personal client visits, telephone selling, group selling, territory and account management, plus participation in technical and professional associations.  Responsible for developing driving the organization thought leadership in the market place through lunch & learns, attending industry events, and facilitating road shoes to show ERS’s thought leadership in the market.

A secondary function will be in the development of other sales personnel.  The Senior Sales Engineer - Technical will be asked to mentor Associate Sales Engineers, Inside Sales Engineers or Sales Engineers in the technical aspects, sales skills, marketing functions, business related activities and other skill sets required of field Sales Engineers.

The anticipated salary range for this role in the Chicago locality is between $120,000 to $148,000 per year

Responsibilities:

- Perform sales support to consistently meet overall area sales goals.

- Make regular sales calls on existing major accounts and establish contact with new accounts.

- Make effective customer presentations, proposal pricing is accurate and technically correct.

- Strength in selling maintenance, engineering services and professional services are required.

- Develop new accounts, sell national accounts and make sales calls at the VP level.

- Perform marketing support to promote the Company’s image throughout the industry.

- Implement area-marketing plan on a monthly basis.

- Assist Corporate needs in new service assessments, marketing research and literature development.

- Perform public relations to promote sales.

- Active participation in trade shows and professional societies.

- Must be able to give effective group presentations for both internal and external customers.

- Member of the Area Management Committee.

- Actively participate as a committee member.

- Assist in the development of the area sales and marketing plan.

- Bring input and new ideas on Sales and Marketing activities.

- Act as mentor and trainer to new sales associates in the fundamentals of Company sales.

- Required to assess the initial skill level and technical expertise of the new sales associate and provide to the regional manager a recommended sales training schedule.

- Training will be provided in the areas of technical assistance, sales skills, walk-through requirements, drawing take-offs, proposal development, and territorial and account management to the new sales associate.

Competencies

To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies:

- Customer Focus – Is dedicated to meeting the expectations and requirements of internal and external customer; Gets first-hand customer information and uses it for improvements in products and services; Acts with customers in mind; Establishes and maintains effective relationships with customers and gains their trust and respect.

- Drive for Results – Can be counted on to exceed goals successfully; is constantly and consistently one of the top performers; very bottom line oriented; steadfastly pushes self and others for results.

- Interpersonal Savvy -  Relates well to all kinds of people, up, down and sideways, inside and outside the organization; builds appropriate rapport; listens; builds constructive and effective relationships; uses diplomacy and tact; truly values people; can diffuse tension.

- Listening – Practices attentive and active listening; has the patience to hear people out; can accurately restate the opinions of others even when he/she disagrees.

- Negotiating – Can negotiate skillfully in tough situations with both internal and external groups; can settle differences with minimum noise; can win concessions without damaging relationships; can be both direct and forceful as well as diplomatic; gains trust quickly.

- Time Management – Uses his/her time effectively and efficiently; sets priorities; values time; separates the critical few from the trivial many and concentrates his/her efforts accordingly.

Education & Certifications:

- Graduate engineer (BSEE/BSME) and no experience; OR

- Graduate of electrical technical school or equivalent, and five years of similar work; OR

- High school diploma or equivalent and eight years of similar work.

Requirements:

- Willing to work flexible hours, weekends, some overnight travel to cover sales territory.

- Regularly required to sit, stand, walk, use hands and fingers, talk and hear.  Required to sit and work at computer.  Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.  Conduct walk-through of construction sites and work in and around electrical equipment.

- Valid Driver’s License required.

TRAVEL TIME REQUIRED

- 50%

THE VERTIV OPPORTUNITY

The successful candidate will embrace Vertiv's Core Principles & Behaviors to help execute our Strategic Priorities.

Our Core Principles: Safety | Integrity | Respect | Teamwork | Inclusion

Full-Time Employment:

The anticipated salary range for this role in Ohio and Illinois locality is between $119,922-$149,840 per year; salary ranges for other geographic localities may vary. Certain roles are eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, annual bonus and stock. These awards are allocated based on individual performance and are role based. In addition, certain roles also have the opportunity to earn sales incentives based on revenue or utilization, depending on the terms of the plan and the employee’s role. The role is eligible to participate in a comprehensive and competitive benefits program, including medical, dental, vision, disability, PTO, holiday pay, and 401k. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process.

Our Strategic Priorities

- High-Performance Culture

- Customer Focus

- Innovation

Vertiv Behaviors

Vertiv (NYSE: VRT) brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to enable its customers' vital applications to run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs. jobs.title: Product Line Project Manager, Global Procurement
jobs.description:
The Product Line Project Manager executes Vertiv’s NPDI (New Product Development and Introduction) process end-to-end for assigned product lines. Reporting into the central program management group while embedded within product line engineering teams, this role manages cross-functional project teams through the full 7-gate process—from concept approval through market introduction and project closure—covering all business units.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Lead NPDI projects through all seven phases and gates: Approve Idea → Approve Concept → Approve Development → Approve Launch → Approve Market Introduction → Approve Business Performance → Approve Project Closure

- Manage cross-functional project teams spanning Engineering, Operations, Procurement, Advanced Manufacturing, Services, and Global Offering Management

- Own the project schedule, gate deliverables, and advancement checklists in Smartsheet; maintain the standard Smartsheet directory and SharePoint structure

- Execute the Product Cost Process using standard templates; track actual vs. target cost and Max Cost targets at each gate milestone

- Manage the Business Case Calculator (BCC) and revenue model; ensure Revenue, Margin, VCM, Gross Margin, Product Cost, Price, and Volume metrics are on track

- Coordinate with Procurement NPDI Leads on Strategic Sourcing Analysis, BOM Health Scorecards, and Single/Sole Source mitigation plans

- Provision new projects: name, number, Smartsheet directory, SharePoint site, dashboard, contact lists, and standard schedule

- Manage project risks, issues, and action items; maintain a current Risk & Issues Log and escalate blockers to program leadership

- Coordinate Technology Readiness Level (TRL) assessments with engineering teams at key gate transitions

- Support manufacturing readiness planning and SIOP demand forecasting as products approach commercial launch

- Report project status to product line leaders and central PMO leadership; present at gate review meetings

- Drive continuous improvement in NPDI process tools, templates, and governance standards

Qualifications :

- Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Operations, or related field; MBA preferred

- 5–8 years of project management experience in product development, engineering, or manufacturing environments

- Demonstrated experience managing stage-gate or phase-gate product development processes end-to-end

- Proficiency with Smartsheet, MS Project, or equivalent project management tools

- Experience with cross-functional team leadership across engineering, procurement, operations, and commercial functions

- Strong knowledge of BOM management, product costing methodologies, and supply chain readiness activities

- Experience in Power, Thermal, IT Systems, or critical infrastructure industries preferred

- PMP certification required; NPDP or Lean/Six Sigma certification preferred

- Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and executive presentation skills; ability to manage multiple concurrent projects

#LI-DR2


The Product Line Project Manager executes Vertiv’s NPDI (New Product Development and Introduction) process end-to-end for assigned product lines. Reporting into the central program management group while embedded within product line engineering teams, this role manages cross-functional project teams through the full 7-gate process—from concept approval through market introduction and project closure—covering all business units.

jobs.title: Regional Sales Manager, Channel (Midwest)
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Sr. Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is responsible for driving growth of Vertiv Rack Solutions - specifically Great Lakes Case & Cabinet offerings through direct engagement with end users, channel partners, and local Vertiv offices within the assigned territory. This role focuses on expanding rack share in data center, SLED, and enterprise environments while creating pull through for complementary Vertiv solutions including rPDU, UPS, thermal, and services. The Sr. RSM will lead regional go to market strategy, develop partner capability, and influence key decision makers across IT, facilities, engineering, and procurement.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Develop, present, and execute a strategic territory business plan that aligns to Vertiv growth objectives for Great Lakes rack solutions.

- Drive incremental revenue through channel partners, distributors, and direct engagement with end users.

- Maintain balanced focus on both existing accounts and new logo acquisition (50/50 mix).

- Build and manage a healthy pipeline within CRM through collaboration with local Vertiv offices and partners.

- Engage and navigate all levels of end user organizations including executives, IT leadership, facility managers, and project teams.

- Conduct site walks aligned with edge and key accelerated compute initiatives, support solution scoping and design collaboration with SE resources.

- Develop a decision maker matrix, account plans, and go to market strategy for key verticals.

- Lead and support partner development activities including training, enablement, and joint selling motions.

- Manage and influence Channel Account Managers (dotted line reporting) within local Vertiv offices to ensure alignment and effective execution.

- Strengthen relationships with regional and national distribution partners supporting Great Lakes rack products.

- Drive partner performance, competencies, and market engagement across the territory.

- Maintain accurate pricing, forecasting, activity reporting, and funnel management.

- Provide consistent feedback to leadership regarding competitive trends, wins/losses, and product needs.

- Coordinate activities with Inside Sales Representatives to maximize visibility and closure of key rack opportunities.

- Support regional trade show strategy, including event selection, logistics, and coverage.

- Ensure timely, high quality customer engagement and post sales follow up to maintain strong customer satisfaction and long-term loyalty.

- Train and mentor less qualified team members as needed.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor’s degree in business, sales, marketing, or related field (or equivalent combination of education and experience).

- 10+ years of sales experience.

- Proven experience in data center, IT infrastructure, or related markets.

- Demonstrated ability to manage a territory with heavy partner and end user engagement.

-  Strong communication skills (written, verbal, and visual media).

-  Able to lead multiple offices, partners, and projects simultaneously in a matrixed environment.

-  Ability to build strong relationships with IT, facilities, engineering, and procurement stakeholders.

-  Highly organized with strong pipeline discipline, forecasting accuracy, and follow-through.

-  Excellent problem-solving abilities and capable of resolving contract and product issues.

-  Ability to adapt quickly to changing market needs and internal processes.

- Willingness to travel extensively across the assigned territory

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Working knowledge of the data center channel ecosystem.

- Experience selling into Fortune 500, enterprise, SLED, and colocation customers.

- Understanding of rack systems, rPDUs, UPS, thermal, and edge infrastructure environments.

- Familiarity with Vertiv’s representative model and product ecosystem..

PHYSICAL & ENVIRONMENTAL DEMANDS

- No special physical requirements.
