jobs.title: Global Category Manager, Global Procurement
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Global Category Manager (GCM) owns the supply panel strategy, category economics, and supplier management for assigned categories across all regions. The role is the single source of truth for category cost models, supplier segmentation, and long-term commercial frameworks — driving should-cost discipline, demand aggregation, and supply panel governance. The GCM coordinates across Product Line Leaders and Regional Category Managers to ensure category strategies are aligned to product roadmaps, NPI timelines, and enterprise cost targets.

Within the global procurement team, this role serves as the category strategy owner — setting the multi-year supply market vision, governing the supplier panel, and driving should-cost discipline across all assigned category spend.

Responsibilities

- Own supply panel strategy: ASL governance, dual-source qualification, demand aggregation, and supplier consolidation across all assigned category spend.

- Govern long-term commercial frameworks (LTAs, MSAs, SOWs, capacity reservations, and commodity hedging) -  transitioning to outcome-based contracting.

- Coordinate with Procurement Product Line Leaders to drive early NPI engagement at Gate 0–1.

- Own supplier innovation partnerships: Advanced Technology Partner (ATP) engagements, technology pipelines, and co-investment strategies with key suppliers.

- Drive cost model governance: should-cost discipline, TCO frameworks, and supplier cost challenge across all category spend.

- Oversee supply panel diversification: alternate source qualification to eliminate single-source risk and regional panel coordination for commercial alignment.

- Own Supplier Code of Conduct and Responsible Business compliance across all assigned category spend.

- Drive supplier segmentation: Strategic / Critical / Important / Transactional.

- Lead supplier negotiations and ensure competitive commercial terms across all regions.

- Implement robust supplier performance management frameworks covering cost, quality, delivery, and innovation.

Qualifications

- 12+ years of experience in procurement, category management, or supply chain within a global, multi-national organization.

- Proven track record in category strategy development and execution across complex global supply bases.

- Experience managing global supplier relationships, including LTA negotiation, supplier development, and performance management.

- Demonstrated ability to drive cost reduction through should-cost modelling, TCO analysis, and value engineering.

- Strong commercial acumen and negotiation skills at senior supplier level.

- Experience working within matrixed organizations with both vertical and horizontal reporting structures.

- Preferred: experience in power systems, thermal systems, electronics, or industrial technology sectors.

- Preferred: experience integrating procurement into product development (NPDI or equivalent lifecycle processes).

jobs.title: Director, Thermal Chain Technical Business Development
jobs.description:
The Director, Thermal Chain Technical Business Development leads Vertiv’s pre-sales technical engagement for thermal management solutions across global strategic Hyperscale, Neo-Cloud, and MTDC customers. This is a critical role bridging deep thermal domain expertise with customer-facing influence to position Vertiv as the basis of design for cooling architectures in next-generation data centers.

The scope encompasses the full spectrum of thermal solutions — from traditional air-cooled systems (perimeter and in-row cooling) to advanced liquid cooling (direct-to-chip, rear-door heat exchangers, immersion cooling), economizer-based designs, and hybrid thermal architectures. As data center densification accelerates and AI/HPC workloads drive unprecedented heat loads, this role is at the forefront of defining how Vertiv addresses extreme density thermal challenges.

The Technical Business Development team positions Vertiv as a trusted partner through deep product and solution expertise, industry insight & leadership, and customer consultation to design solutions that meet customers’ unique needs. The goal is to “get up and to the left” – engaging higher in the customer organization to the decision maker level and earlier in the process to position Vertiv as the basis of design.

The incumbent guides a team of thermal domain experts with credible technical capability and strong communication and influence skills. Strong collaboration and partnership with the Hyperscale, Neocloud, and MTDC account managers, data center solutions, power train, and whitespace solutions teams are critical to deliver a consistent and unified message to advance Vertiv’s market position.

This position requires invention on a daily basis with a keen sense of urgency and market approach nimbleness. Today’s data center customers expect speed and technical competence in addressing thermal challenges at scale — particularly as rack densities push beyond 100kW and liquid cooling becomes a baseline requirement.

SUCCESS MEASURES

- Thermal Basis-of-Design: Achievement of Vertiv thermal products/solutions as customer basis-of-design across cooling architectures (air, liquid, hybrid).

- Share-of-Wallet Penetration: Measurable orders & sales share gain for thermal solutions at target GSA customers.

- Thought Leadership: Collaboration with Thermal BU/Product Lines to develop reference cooling architectures and disseminate thermal thought leadership to customers, industry events, and market publications.

- Account Strategy: Collaboration with GSA and NAM Sales counterparts to define and execute thermal-specific growth strategies within overall account plans.

- Capability Maturity: Expansion of team capabilities; evolution from product-specific thermal skills to system-level thermal chain expertise integrated with overall data center architecture.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Customer Technical Engagement:

- Lead technical engagement with identified and emerging GSA customers to influence and design thermal architectures positioning Vertiv’s cooling portfolio as the basis of design.

- Collaborate directly with strategic GSA customers to design overall thermal strategies addressing current and future density requirements.

- Whiteboard system-level thermal architectures with customer CTOs, Engineering, and Design leadership — articulating trade-offs between air-cooled, liquid-cooled, and hybrid approaches.

- Drive early engagement in the customer’s design cycle to shape thermal requirements before RFP issuance.

Product, Systems & Solutions Expertise:

- Deep understanding of Vertiv’s thermal portfolio including precision air cooling, in-row/perimeter units, chillers, economizers, direct liquid cooling (DLC), rear-door heat exchangers, and immersion cooling solutions.

- Ability to articulate system-level thermal design — from chip to atmosphere — including facility water systems, heat rejection, piping infrastructure, and controls integration.

- Ensure technical buyers understand Vertiv’s thermal capabilities; coordinate solution alignment with product roadmaps and drive innovative approaches to meet evolving density and sustainability requirements.

- Drive alignment and collaboration across senior leadership, sales, product development, and engineering to mature and disseminate thermal thought leadership and reference designs. One Vertiv.

- Engage with external design firms and consulting engineers to influence thermal specifications.

Voice-of-Customer (VOC):

- Capture and communicate market needs, product gaps, and emerging thermal trends to the Thermal BU and Product Lines.

- Drive feedback loops to shape future thermal products and solution strategies — particularly around liquid cooling evolution and sustainability requirements.

Industry Engagement:

- Represent Vertiv in trade shows, conferences, and industry publications to showcase thermal technical thought leadership.

- Build visibility into Vertiv’s thermal strategic direction and reinforce its market posture in cooling innovation.

- Engage with industry bodies (ASHRAE, The Green Grid, OCP) on thermal standards and best practices.

Team Leadership & Development:

- Lead and mentor a team of thermal domain experts across assigned regions.

- Foster collaboration, cross-learning, and best-practice sharing across the team and with global peers.

- Build cross-BU technical capabilities within the team (e.g., understanding power and whitespace interdependencies with thermal design).

QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or related discipline; advanced degree (MBA or MS) strongly preferred.

- 10+ years of progressive responsibility in technical business development, thermal/HVAC solution engineering, or pre-sales leadership roles, with at least 5 years at a senior level influencing enterprise customers and shaping thermal solution strategy.

- Recognized expertise in data center thermal management, including both air-cooled and liquid-cooled architectures, with a demonstrable record of steering cooling architecture decisions at global or strategic accounts.

- Demonstrated success translating thermal technical strategies into revenue growth, market share expansion, or measurable business impact. Experience collaborating directly with sales leadership to develop account strategies.

- Deep, hands-on understanding of data center cooling technologies — precision cooling, economization, liquid cooling (DLC, immersion, rear-door), heat rejection systems, and thermal controls — combined with the ability to integrate thermal design within overall data center architecture.

- Experience leading geographically dispersed teams, aligning with global Product Lines and Business Units, and influencing senior executives across engineering, product management, and sales organizations.

- Established presence in industry forums, standards bodies (ASHRAE, OCP), or trade publications; capable of representing Vertiv’s thermal direction credibly at conferences and with analysts.

- Exceptional ability to engage at the C-suite level with customers and to articulate a compelling technical and commercial vision to both internal and external stakeholders.

- Ability to travel extensively to strategic customers, regional teams, and global BU locations.

This role may be performed in multiple jurisdictions. In jurisdictions subject to EU Pay Transparency requirements, a locally applicable salary range applies and will be communicated in accordance with local legal obligations, if not shown in this posting. Salary ranges for other jurisdictions may vary in line with local market conditions and applicable legislation.

This is a critical role bridging deep electrical power domain expertise with customer-facing influence to position Vertiv as the basis of design for power architectures in mission-critical data center environments.

The scope encompasses the full power train — from utility entrance through medium voltage switchgear, transformers, UPS systems (AC and DC), static transfer switches, power distribution (PDUs, RPPs, busway), and battery/energy storage systems. As data center campuses scale to hundreds of megawatts and AI workloads demand unprecedented power density and reliability, this role is at the forefront of defining how Vertiv addresses next-generation power challenges.

The Technical Business Development team positions Vertiv as a trusted partner through deep product and solution expertise, industry insight & leadership, and customer consultation to design solutions that meet customers’ unique needs. The goal is to “get up and to the left” – engaging higher in the customer organization to the decision maker level and earlier in the process to position Vertiv as the basis of design.

The incumbent guides a team of power domain experts with credible technical capability and strong communication and influence skills. Strong collaboration and partnership with the Hyperscale, Neocloud, and MTDC account managers, data center solutions, thermal chain, and whitespace solutions teams are critical to deliver a consistent and unified message to advance Vertiv’s market position.

This position requires invention on a daily basis with a keen sense of urgency and market approach nimbleness. Today’s data center customers expect speed and technical competence in addressing power challenges at scale — particularly as campuses grow to GW-scale and customers explore alternative power architectures including DC distribution and on-site generation.

SUCCESS MEASURES

- Power Basis-of-Design: Achievement of Vertiv power products/solutions as customer basis-of-design across power architectures (AC, DC, hybrid, modular power).

- Share-of-Wallet Penetration: Measurable orders & sales share gain for power train solutions at target GSA customers.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Customer Technical Engagement:

- Lead technical engagement with identified and emerging GSA customers to influence and design power architectures positioning Vertiv’s power portfolio as the basis of design.

- Collaborate directly with strategic GSA customers to design overall power strategies addressing current and future capacity, density, and reliability requirements.

- Whiteboard system-level power architectures with customer CTOs, Engineering, and Design leadership — articulating trade-offs between AC/DC topologies, redundancy levels, and modular vs. traditional approaches.

- Drive early engagement in the customer’s design cycle to shape power requirements before RFP issuance.

Product, Systems & Solutions Expertise:

- Deep understanding of Vertiv’s power portfolio including UPS systems (AC and DC), switchgear, PDUs, RPPs, busway, static transfer switches, battery/energy storage systems, and integrated power modules/skids.

- Ability to articulate system-level power design — from utility entrance to rack — including medium voltage infrastructure, paralleling, distribution topologies, monitoring/controls, and power quality.

- Understanding of Vertiv’s integrated power solutions such as OneCore and power modules/skids to steer opportunities toward Vertiv’s differentiated offerings.

- Ensure technical buyers understand Vertiv’s power capabilities; coordinate solution alignment with product roadmaps and drive innovative approaches to meet evolving capacity, efficiency, and sustainability requirements.

- Drive alignment and collaboration across senior leadership, sales, product development, and engineering to mature and disseminate power train thought leadership and reference designs. One Vertiv.

- Engage with external design firms and consulting engineers to influence power specifications.

Voice-of-Customer (VOC):

- Capture and communicate market needs, product gaps, and emerging power trends to the Power BU and Product Lines.

- Drive feedback loops to shape future power products and solution strategies — particularly around DC architectures, energy storage evolution, grid integration, and sustainability requirements.

Industry Engagement:

- Represent Vertiv in trade shows, conferences, and industry publications to showcase power train technical thought leadership.

- Build visibility into Vertiv’s power strategic direction and reinforce its market posture in power innovation.

- Engage with industry bodies (IEEE, NFPA, Uptime Institute) on power standards and best practices.

Team Leadership & Development:

- Lead and mentor a team of power domain experts across assigned regions.

- Foster collaboration, cross-learning, and best-practice sharing across the team and with global peers.

- Build cross-BU technical capabilities within the team (e.g., understanding thermal and whitespace interdependencies with power design).

QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems Engineering, or related discipline; advanced degree (MBA or MS) strongly preferred.

- 10+ years of progressive responsibility in technical business development, power systems/electrical solution engineering, or pre-sales leadership roles, with at least 5 years at a senior level influencing enterprise customers and shaping power solution strategy.

- Recognized expertise in data center power infrastructure, including UPS, distribution, and energy storage architectures, with a demonstrable record of steering power architecture decisions at global or strategic accounts.

- Demonstrated success translating power technical strategies into revenue growth, market share expansion, or measurable business impact. Experience collaborating directly with sales leadership to develop account strategies.

- Deep, hands-on understanding of data center power technologies — UPS (AC/DC), switchgear, PDUs, busway, STS, battery/BESS systems, and power monitoring/controls — combined with the ability to integrate power design within overall data center architecture.

- Experience leading geographically dispersed teams, aligning with global Product Lines and Business Units, and influencing senior executives across engineering, product management, and sales organizations.

- Established presence in industry forums, standards bodies (IEEE, NFPA, Uptime Institute), or trade publications; capable of representing Vertiv’s power direction credibly at conferences and with analysts.

- Exceptional ability to engage at the C-suite level with customers and to articulate a compelling technical and commercial vision to both internal and external stakeholders.

- Ability to travel extensively to strategic customers, regional teams, and global BU locations.

jobs.title: Product Line Leader, Global Procurement
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Procurement Product Line Leader owns end-to-end procurement execution for assigned product lines within a Business unit vertical, with accountability for cost performance, supplier delivery, and NPI procurement readiness. The role bridges category strategy — set by Global Category Managers (GCMs) — with product-line-specific execution, ensuring procurement is embedded in product development, engineering changes, and production ramp activities. The Product Line Leader is the primary procurement interface to Product Management and Engineering for their assigned product lines.

Within the global procurement operating model, this role operates as the product-line procurement execution owner — translating GCM category strategies into product-line-specific sourcing actions, owning NPI procurement milestones, and driving cost-out programmes aligned to product P&L targets.

Responsibilities

•  Own procurement execution for assigned product lines: cost targets, supplier delivery performance, and material availability aligned to production schedules.

•  Drive NPI procurement readiness: early engagement at Gate 0–1, supplier quote coverage, tooling investment decisions, and production ramp sourcing plans.

•  Translate global  category strategies into product-line-specific sourcing actions and supplier selections, ensuring alignment with approved supply panels.

•  Own product-line cost-out programmes: value engineering, specification optimisation, and make-vs-buy analysis in partnership with Engineering.

•  Manage day-to-day supplier performance for product-line-critical suppliers: delivery, quality, capacity, and escalation management.

•  Partner with Engineering and Product Management as the primary procurement interface for all product-line decisions affecting cost, supply, and schedule.

•  Drive engineering change management from a procurement perspective: cost impact assessment, supplier feasibility analysis, and lead-time implications.

•  Support the BU Leader in delivering BU savings targets through product-line-level cost reduction initiatives and continuous improvement programmes.

•  Coordinate with GCMs on supplier panel utilisation, ensuring product-line sourcing is aligned with globally negotiated commercial frameworks and approved ASLs.

•  Own product-line procurement KPIs: material cost variance, supplier on-time delivery (OTD), NPI milestone adherence, and cost-out pipeline value.

Qualifications

•  10+ years of experience in procurement, supply chain, or sourcing within a manufacturing or industrial technology environment.

•  Proven experience managing procurement for specific product lines or business units with direct accountability for cost and delivery performance.

•  Demonstrated ability to integrate procurement into new product development processes (NPDI or equivalent lifecycle frameworks).

•  Experience in supplier management, including performance monitoring, escalation handling, and supplier development programmes.

•  Strong cross-functional collaboration skills with Engineering, Product Management, and Operations teams.

•  Commercial acumen with hands-on experience in cost modelling, value engineering, and make-vs-buy analysis.

•  Preferred: experience in power systems, thermal systems, electronics, or industrial technology sectors.

jobs.title: Human Resources Business Partner
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

We are seeking an experienced and proactive HR Business Partner to join the Human Resources team supporting the Americas region. In this role, you will serve as a trusted advisor to engineering managers and leaders across our ER&D Business Units on all matters related to human resources.

You should be a proactive communicator and change agent who can balance employee advocacy with business objectives to create integrated solutions in a high-growth engineering environment. HRBP duties include extensive employee relations skills, problem solving, conflict resolution, and coaching. You will partner with ER&D leadership in developing a culture supportive of company values, and drive communication, recognition, and rewards to strengthen employee engagement.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Serve as the primary employee relations point of contact, managing employee relations cases including intake, investigation, documentation, and resolution.

- Proactively coach engineering managers on people management challenges — conflict resolution, performance concerns, team dynamics, and policy interpretation.

- Partner with hiring managers and talent acquisition on the recruitment process, including job profile development, candidate assessment, and selection decision-making.

- Own new hire offer alignment, ensuring internal equity, appropriate leveling, and consistency with compensation guidelines.

- Coordinate and drive the performance management cycle for assigned client groups.

- Partner with managers on Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) development, documentation, and follow-up cadence.

- Assess and coach managers and employees to achieve maximum performance.

- Assist with benchmarking analysis and develop recommendations for new hires, promotions, transfers, and merit plan documentation.

- Partner with talent management to address organizational development needs and facilitate individual or custom learning solutions as determined by engineering leadership.

- Ensure compliance with regional employment laws, company policies, and HR processes.

Minimum Qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related field; Master's degree preferred

- 3–5 years of progressive HR experience with previous exposure to learning and development or equivalent practical experience

- Demonstrated experience with employee relations case management

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)

Preferred Qualifications:

- Thorough understanding of human resources principles

- Working knowledge of HRIS systems and HR analytics/reporting tools

- Ability to clearly communicate with employees, applicants, and leadership — both verbally and in writing — to represent the HR function professionally

- Willingness to work flexible hours, occasional travel to local Americas sites, and adapt to a fast-paced, high-growth environment

jobs.title: Human Resources Leadership Development Program (2027)
jobs.description:
The mission of Vertiv’s Human Resources Leadership Development Program (HRLDP) is to create the Organization’s next HR Leaders by developing new industry talent – providing them exposure to multiple facets of Human Resources through rotational experiences, professional support from dedicated mentor, and opportunities for cross-program collaboration. HRLDP participants will take on meaningful assignments that build strategic, operational, and leadership capabilities, while also gaining visibility with senior leaders across the organization.

As an HRLDP participant, you won't just learn about HR—you’ll shape. You’ll take on meaningful, high-impact assignments that build your strategic, operational, and leadership capabilities while gaining direct visibility with senior leaders across our global organization.

HOW HRLDP WORKS

The HRLDP provides recent master graduates with the opportunity to attain hands on experience in different areas of Human Resources at a global, multi-billion-dollar organization.

The program will consist of three, one-year rotations designed to accelerate your growth and give you broad HR expertise.

Rotations may include experiences in:

- Center of Excellence (e.g., Talent Management, Compensation, Learning & Development)

- Global HR (partnering with business leaders on organizational strategy)

- Plant HR (supporting employees and operations at a manufacturing site)

- Participants also have the unique opportunity to complete a rotation outside of Westerville, Ohio—either at another U.S. location or internationally —expanding your perspective and preparing you for global leadership roles.

- Throughout the program, you will receive ongoing professional development opportunities, including workshops, training, and exposure to senior leadership

- Each participant is paired with a dedicated mentor who provides guidance, coaching, and support throughout the program

Who We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate is a motivated and collaborative individual who thrives in dynamic environments, embraces change, and is passionate about developing people and organizations.

Preferred Experience & Skills

- Internship or work experience in Human Resources, Talent Management, or related areas

- Demonstrated ability to build relationships and influence stakeholders at multiple levels

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

- Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.

QUALIFICATIONS

- Master’s degree in human resources, Organizational Psychology, Human Resource Development, Business Administration, or related field

- At least one relevant HR internship or 1 year of related professional experience

jobs.title: Country Partner Manager
jobs.description:
Brief Job Description:

The Partner Manager is responsible for sales growth through managed reseller and distributor partners to help maximize channel sales opportunities across the region.

The main contribution of this role is driving aggressive revenue growth of Mission-Critical infrastructure solutions from Vertiv’s Rack and Edge based products, including UPS, Rack/Row based Cooling, Power Distribution and IT Management portfolios.

Mission-critical infrastructure solutions include:

- Hardware – 1-phase and 3-phase uninterruptible power supplies, racks, power distribution, thermal management (air and liquid cooling) and remote IT management.

- Software – power & thermal management control, remote access & control of IT assets, user based access & visualization management, protocol interface & standards for IT / facilities management / DCIM / BMS systems.

- Services – extended warranty, commissioning and maintenance packages, as well as mechanical / electrical installation, project management, integration, assembly and ancillary services specific to critical infrastructure environments.

Customer Focus:

- Account focus will be on a diversified IT reseller & distribution segment, with focus on projects requiring infrastructure to support white space IT hardware and High Performance Computing applications, housing AI compute chipsets and servers.

- End users and technology service providers, ranging from SME space to global Blue Chip companies and government entities covering a full breadth of market verticals.

- Channel Partners, ranging from server OEMs to large IT resellers, working in tandem with our Electrical Distribution   partner network.

Responsibilities and Measurement Criteria with Time investment Needed on Each: -

(This will describe the overall core responsibilities of the role, decision making responsibilities etc.)

- Create and manage agreed partner business (growth) plans. Setting targets for Partner Incentive Agreements and working to achieve / exceed agreed sales targets and KPI commitments.

- Identify, recruit, onboard and progress partners through the Vertiv Partner Program.

- On site cadence to develop the technical competency of each partner and support sales enablement, whilst utilizing resources including Application Engineering, Marketing and Sales Support.

- Along with other joint resources, roll out promotional activity, product launches and plan partner events, such as technology workshops and seminars.

- Monthly and Quarterly business reviews with stakeholders.

- Perform site surveys to scope and qualify customer technical and commercial requirements.

- Selecting product mixes, developing solutions and managing quotations.

- Facilitating bid management, through Vertiv’s Quote to Order process: Provide effective qualification of opportunities, use of Vertiv’s configuration / quote tools, and work to manage customer expectations through Vertiv’s Application Engineering team to provide technically and commercially comprehensive bids.

- Extensive and professional use of CRM tools. Supporting Vertiv’s management standards ensuring high quality, accurate input to pipeline management and forecasting.

- Manage all additional account management functions such as operations, stock control and contact management.

- Support demonstrations, planning and accompanying partners / end users both domestically and internationally.

- Channel conflict management.

- Deal registration and Special Price Request (SPR) management.

- Lead and coordinate marketing plans, promotions and product launches, along with channel field marketing functions.

- Champion Vertiv tools and programs such as the Vertiv Partner Program, Partner Portal and Vertiv Solution Designer.

- Identify, develop and maintain relationships with Vertiv funded heads in the reseller network.

Qualifications: -

Required/ Minimum Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree in an applicable technology or business field, with demonstrated business aptitude.

- Excellent people management and relationship building skills.

- Excellent presentation and verbal / written communication skills, delivered in person and via virtual settings.

- Exceptionally strong channel development and management experience of at least 5+ years in similar or related positions with strong understanding of regional resellers and partners in the region.

- Outstanding, demonstratable track record in achieving sales targets.

- International English at advanced level.

- Significant experience managing sales, or multiple component products / programs.

- Experience in use of PowerBI reports to impart customer insight and facilitate internal reporting requirements.

- Familiarity with sales channels including IT Distribution, Electrical Distribution, Value Added Resellers, System Integrators, and Electrical & Mechanical Contractors is essential.

- Familiarity with technology verticals including IT cloud services, communication / telecom, collocation and enterprise is highly preferred.

- Familiarity with server OEM & ODM market leaders, their technologies, capabilities, go-to-market routes, and strategies is highly preferred.

Additional / Preferred Qualifications:

- Demonstrating Ethics and Integrity: Increase Vertiv’s market share and achieve / exceed budget figures in line with company ethics and policy. You follow through with promises. You use ethical considerations to guide decision and actions, conforming with regulatory compliance and ITC.

-  Building and Maintaining Relationships: You negotiate adeptly with individuals and groups. You are effective at managing conflict and confrontations skillfully. You know how to build and maintain working relationships with co-employees and external parties.

- You are a driven self-starter with a sense of urgency: an ability to plan, organize and manage time effectively, whilst developing / executing strategic business plans. You are analytical and enjoy problem solving.

- Contribute to teamwork and knowledge sharing inside the team and organization: maintain and update reporting systems, run scheduled and ad-hoc analysis, lead and participate in team meetings and share your experiences, share new knowledge you gather about the market, competitors and challenges you perceive we face.

- Focus on self-growth and development: keep an open mind and learn from some of the best experts in the industry, participate in Vertiv meetings and events to acquire knowledge of where the market is going, keep up to date with technical developments, participate in company trainings and apply the knowledge in your day-to-day work.

- Be innovative: bring your own ideas of improvements inside the team, look at each process and task with the goal of constantly improving it to bring more value to the customer, to you, the team, and the organization.

Physical & Environmental Requirements: - (To be used majorly for manufacturing jobs.)

- None

Time Travel Needed:

- 70% travel expected on average, with prolonged peaks on occasion.

jobs.title: Finance Leadership Development Program
jobs.description:
Job Description

POSITION SUMMARY

Location: Westerville, Ohio

Company: Vertiv

VERTIV FINANCE LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM

The mission of Vertiv’s Finance Leadership Development Program (FLDP) is to create the Organization’s next Finance Leaders by developing new industry talent - providing them exposure to multiple facets of the business in a rotational role format, professional support through a pre-designated Mentor, and inner and outer program collaboration. Through this program, FLDP participants will work in several roles throughout the company, acquiring experience, owning key tasks, advancing leadership skills, and gaining exposure to the top levels of leadership in the organization. The program also provides professional development and networking opportunities to grow participant’s future leadership potential. After completion of the three-year program, successful participants will have the opportunity to apply for critical roles within the Global Finance team.

Our Finance Leadership Development Program offers a unique opportunity for talented individuals to immerse themselves in various facets of finance. Over the course of three years, participants will engage in multiple rotations within our Finance function, providing exposure to diverse areas of expertise and fostering a deep understanding of the discipline.

HOW FLDP WORKS

The FLDP provides recent college graduates with the opportunity to attain hands on experience in different areas of Finance at a global, multi-billion-dollar organization.

The program will consist of 3 one-year rotations covering different financial disciplines, including:

- Manufacturing Accounting

- Financial Planning & Analysis

- Treasury

- Internal Audit

- External Reporting

- Investor Relations

- Operational Accounting

APPLICANTS

The right candidate for this program will be a dynamic individual who is excited by challenges, embraces change, and is eager to learn and work at fast pace.

Qualifications

-  Finance or Accounting internship experience

-  Ability to develop and articulate general strategies and detailed operation plans

- Proven track record of delivering commitments and working effectively with peers outside the Finance function

-  Proficient in spreadsheets, databases, MS Office, Oracle, Hyperion Financial Management and financial software applications

- Bachelor of Science in Business: Specialization in Business Administration, Finance, or Accounting

- Minimum of one relevant internship and/or 1 year of experience

- Demonstrated strong work ethic

- Highly efficient and detail-oriented

- Strong analytical skills or ability to organize and digest large sets of data with minimal instruction

Recommended

- Minimum GPA of 3.0

- Relevant internship or previous experience in Finance/Accounting

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Reports to: Global Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)

Job Summary

The Director of Global GRC is a critical leadership role responsible for the design, implementation, and management of Vertiv’s information security Governance, Risk Management, and Compliance function. You will serve as the primary architect of our IT Risk Register and the lead coordinator for IT General Controls (ITGC) and SOX compliance.

As a global leader, you will manage a geographically dispersed team, ensuring a unified and aware security posture. This role requires extensive systems knowledge, soft skills, executive presence capable of driving consensus across a diverse, international stakeholder base. It also requires fierce program ownership and accountability.

Key Responsibilities

- Global Team Leadership: Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing, globally dispersed GRC team. Foster a culture of accountability and follow-through and collaboration across different time zones, languages, and cultural work styles.

- Customer & Sales Enablement: Lead the global process for responding to customer security questionnaires. Maintain, improve and finalize a centralized "Trust Center" to accelerate the sales cycle globally.

- Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM): Build and scale a global vendor risk program covering both Direct and Indirect procurement, ensuring consistency in how we vet global suppliers.

- IT Risk & Vulnerability Governance: Manage the Enterprise IT Risk Register. Translate technical vulnerabilities (scans/pen tests) into business risk terms and remediation trackers for IT leaders.

- SOX & IT General Controls (ITGC): Lead the ITGC program in collaboration with Internal Audit. Ensure Vertiv remains compliant with SOX requirements through continuous monitoring of global controls.

- Security Awareness & Training: Own the global security training strategy, ensuring training materials are culturally relevant and localized where necessary.

- Pentest & Audit Oversight: Serve as the central point of contact for all global security audits. Oversee the tracking and closure of remediation items across all business units.

- Governance Committee Leadership: Lead our Cyber Risk Oversight Committee which is the primary forum for discussing Enterprise Cyber and Compliance risk.

Required Skills & Qualifications

- Experience: 10+ years in Information Security, with 5+ years in a dedicated GRC leadership role.

- Global Leadership: Proven experience managing and scaling globally dispersed teams. Must demonstrate success in leading remote subordinates and maintaining high engagement across disparate geographic regions.

- Regulatory Knowledge: Deep expertise in SOX (ITGC) controls and procedures , NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and GDPR.

- Risk Methodology: Proven track record of managing an Enterprise Risk Register and applying risk-quantification frameworks (e.g., FAIR or NIST 800-30).

- Communication: Exceptional ability to communicate complex security risks to non-technical stakeholders across the globe.

- Strategy, Organization and Accountability: Top notch skills in assessing current state, devilment of roadmap and actions in a qualitative and quantitative manner aligned with CMMI.

- Travel:Ability to travel internationally  to Vertiv’s global offices and regional hubs to conduct internal reviews, meet with regional leaders, and support audit activities.

- Certifications: CISM, CRISC, CISA, or CISSP.

- Tooling: Experience implementing GRC platforms (e.g., ServiceNow GRC, OneTrust) on a global scale.

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or Sciences,  or related field; Master's preferred.

JOB DESCRIPTION

LOCATION
Thane, India / Regional Scope

8-12 years

Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering
FUNCTION
Strategic Sourcing / Commodity Management

Position Summary

The Regional Commodity Manager for Liquid cooling SFN is responsible for developing and executing regional sourcing strategies for SS Pipe/Flange/Fittings/Valve/Sensor/Other Mechanical Commodity. Proven experience in handling contract manufacturing and outsourcing business within strategic sourcing.

This role will strengthen supplier competitiveness, optimize total cost, protect continuity of supply and support business growth across project-based and operational requirements.

The position serves as the primary commercial interface between SFN suppliers and internal stakeholders, including Engineering, Quality, Operations, Logistics, Sales, Product Management and Global Procurement. The successful candidate will combine Mechanical product knowledge with strong strategic sourcing, negotiation and supplier-management capabilities.

Key Responsibilities 1. Commodity Strategy and Strategic Sourcing

- Develop and execute regional commodity strategies for Pipe/Flange/Fittings/Valve/Sensor/Other Mechanical Commodity etc.

- Align regional plans with global commodity direction, business objectives, technology roadmaps and customer requirements.

- Stainless Steel supplier market scans, RFIs, RFQs, e-sourcing events, bid evaluations, negotiations and sourcing recommendations.

- Identify, qualify and onboard competitive suppliers, including localization and alternate-source opportunities.

- Build should-cost, total-cost-of-ownership and price-benchmarking models to support sourcing decisions.

2. Supplier Relationship and Performance Management

- Establish strategic relationships with manufacturers, system integrators and key sub-tier suppliers.

- Conduct regular supplier business reviews covering quality, cost, delivery, capacity, technology, service and sustainability.

- Develop corrective and improvement plans for underperforming suppliers and track actions to closure.

- Coordinate supplier development with Quality and Engineering to improve process capability, reliability and responsiveness.

3. Cost, Productivity and Commercial Management

- Deliver annual productivity and cost-reduction programs through negotiation, value engineering, localization, resourcing, specification optimization and supplier consolidation.

- Monitor key cost drivers.

- Negotiate commercial agreements, pricing mechanisms, warranties, payment terms, lead times, logistics models and service obligations.

- Maintain contract coverage and ensure sourcing decisions comply with delegated authority and procurement governance.

4. Supply Continuity and Risk Management

- Assess supplier capacity, financial health, geographic concentration, logistics exposure, sub-tier dependency and raw-material risks.

- Create and maintain mitigation plans, including dual sourcing, safety-stock arrangements, local warehousing, capacity reservation and business-continuity actions.

- Partner with planning, operations and suppliers to resolve shortages, expedite critical requirements and protect customer commitments.

- Monitor market developments and provide timely risk and opportunity updates to leadership.

5. Cross-Functional and Technical Collaboration

- Engage early in new product introduction, customer proposals and engineering change activities to ensure competitive and supply-ready solutions.

- Work with Engineering and Quality on specifications, supplier qualification, testing, approvals, reliability, warranty and failure-resolution activities.

- Support standardization and rationalization of makes, models and configurations across business units and sites.

- Coordinate with Sales and Product Management to understand pipeline, project timing, technology needs and regional customer expectations.

6. Sustainability, Compliance and Governance

- Ensure suppliers comply with applicable environmental, health and safety, trade, ethical sourcing and regulatory requirements.

- Promote responsible sourcing, recycling, end-of-life management, safe transportation and reduced environmental impact.

- Maintain accurate sourcing records, approvals, contracts, supplier data and audit documentation.

7. Analytics and Reporting

- Maintain commodity dashboards covering spend, savings, quality, delivery, lead time, inventory, contract coverage and supplier risk.

- Prepare periodic commodity reviews, executive updates and sourcing pipeline reports.

- Use data to identify supply-base, working-capital, cost and service improvement opportunities.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering.

- 8-12 years of experience in strategic sourcing, commodity management, procurement, supplier development or supply chain roles.

- Demonstrated experience sourcing of Mechanical products/Components.

- Experience working in a project-based, engineered-to-order or high-mix, low-volume business environment is preferred.

- Strong commercial negotiation, contract management, analytical and stakeholder-management skills.

- Ability to read and interpret drawings specifications, drawings, data sheets, test requirements and supplier technical proposals.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and ERP/procurement systems; experience with Power BI or similar analytics tools is preferred.

- Fluent business English and willingness to travel regionally/globally as required.

Key Performance Indicators

- Cost savings and productivity delivery

- Supplier on-time delivery and lead-time improvement

- Supplier quality and corrective-action closure

- Localization and alternate-source implementation

- Contract coverage and sourcing compliance

- Inventory and working-capital improvement

- Supplier risk reduction and continuity readiness

- Project sourcing milestones and stakeholder satisfaction

- ESG and supplier-compliance performance

Preferred Industry Exposure

Candidates with sourcing or engineering exposure in the following sectors will be preferred:

- Thermal/HVAC/Liquid cooling

- Data centers/ Large Infra companies/Turnkey Project

- Manufacturing thermal cooling equipment

- Oil & Gas/Energy/petrochemical/ Heavy Fabrication

- Automobile

Role Success Profile

The ideal candidate is a technically credible and commercially strong sourcing professional who can translate business demand into a clear commodity strategy, create competitive supplier options and deliver measurable improvements in cost, quality, delivery and supply resilience. The person should be comfortable operating across regional and global teams, managing ambiguity and influencing decisions without direct authority.

Note:  The responsibilities and qualifications may be adjusted based on business needs, regional scope and organizational structure.

jobs.title: EMEA Demand Planning Specialist - Digital Transformation
jobs.description:
Who are we?

At Vertiv, we’re on a mission to empower the people that will power the future. From a simple swipe to life-changing medicines, from push notifications to generative AI. We design, manufacture, and service the products and solutions that keep the world connected.  With $6.9 billion in sales, a strong customer base and global reach spanning nearly 70 countries, we are uniquely positioned to deliver greater value to our customers and create new opportunities for our people.

We are now looking for an EMEA Demand Planning Specialist - Digital Transformation in Cluj-Napoca, Romania!

The EMEA Demand Planning Specialist - Digital Transformation serves as the functional Demand Planning Subject Matter Expert for the EMEA Kinaxis Maestro rollout. The role supports the design, testing, deployment, adoption, and continuous improvement of standardized Demand Planning capabilities across EMEA.

Working across business stakeholders, Global Process Owners, IT, and implementation partners, the specialist ensures that regional requirements are represented in the solution and that Kinaxis enables improved forecast quality, planning efficiency, and SIOP decision-making.

Position Summary

Reporting to the EMEA Senior Manager, Digital Transformation, this senior individual contributor combines deep Demand Planning expertise with strong analytical, project, change, and stakeholder-management capabilities. The role has no direct reports and provides functional leadership through expertise and influence.

Key Responsibilities Demand Planning Process Design & Standardization

- Act as the EMEA Demand Planning SME for Kinaxis Maestro and represent EMEA requirements in global design workshops.

- Support the future-state Demand Planning operating model, including processes, governance, calendars, roles, and decision rights.

- Drive standardization and alignment across Demand Planning, SIOP, S&OE, Supply Planning, Inventory, Production Planning, and Materials Management.

Kinaxis Maestro Deployment

- Validate workflows, planning hierarchies, dashboards, alerts, exceptions, assumptions, and scenario capabilities.

- Lead or coordinate user acceptance testing, defect validation, business sign-off, readiness, cutover, go-live, hypercare, and stabilization.

Forecasting & Performance

- Support adoption of statistical forecasting, demand sensing, AI/ML forecasting, segmentation, exception management, and forecast-value-add analysis.

- Enable integration of customer forecasts, commercial intelligence, pipeline opportunities, orders, product lifecycle events, and market assumptions.

- Monitor forecast accuracy, bias, forecast value add, cycle adherence, adoption, and process compliance; coordinate corrective actions.

Change Management & Continuous Improvement

- Deliver training and coaching and build an effective EMEA super-user network.

- Drive adoption, identify process or system enhancements, and support realization of transformation benefits.

Qualifications & Experience Required

- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, Engineering, Economics, Information Systems, or a related field.

- 5+ years of experience in Demand Planning, Forecasting, SIOP/IBP, or broader supply chain planning.

- Strong knowledge of forecasting methodologies, consensus planning, scenario planning, and performance measurement.

- Experience in a multinational manufacturing environment and in a planning-process or advanced-planning-system transformation.

- Ability to translate business requirements into process and system requirements.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, facilitation, communication, documentation, and stakeholder-management skills.

- Full professional proficiency in English.

Preferred

- Hands-on experience with Kinaxis Maestro / RapidResponse or another advanced planning platform such as SAP APO/IBP, Oracle Planning, Blue Yonder, or o9.

- Experience with statistical forecasting, AI/ML forecasting, demand sensing, exception-based planning, and Power BI or similar analytics tools.

- APICS CPIM/CSCP or comparable certification.

The successful candidate will embrace Vertiv’s Core Principals & Behaviors to help execute our Strategic Priorities.

OUR STRATEGIC PRIORITIES

- Customer Focus

- Operational Excellence

- High-Performance Culture

- Innovation

- Financial Strength

- Own It

- Act With Urgency

- Foster a Customer-First Mindset

- Think Big and Execute

- Lead by Example

- Drive Continuous Improvement

- Learn and Seek Out Development

At Vertiv, we offer the stability of a global leader in a growing industry and the opportunity of a startup. POSITION SUMMARY:

The Digital Indirect Tax Operations & Automation Analyst (P2) is a mid-level role within the Indirect Tax team, responsible for supporting U.S. indirect tax operations by ensuring accurate sales and use tax determination, maintaining tax compliance, and driving continuous process improvements through automation, AI, and digital solutions.

This role combines traditional indirect tax operational responsibilities with emerging technologies, including workflow automation, AI-enabled productivity tools, process optimization, and data analytics, to enhance operational efficiency and strengthen compliance.

Working closely with the Indirect Tax team and cross-functional stakeholders, the analyst will help identify automation opportunities, streamline manual processes, and support the organization's digital transformation initiatives while building foundational expertise in indirect tax and tax technology.

Key Responsibilities

Functional Expertise

Maintain the customer exemption electronic database, ensuring data integrity and completeness while using automation tools to optimize record management and error-proofing measures.

Validate and maintain accurate supporting documentation for sales transactions, serving as the data foundation for indirect tax compliance and downstream automated workflows.

Support state sales and use tax audits by utilizing data extraction and reconciliation tools to efficiently prepare documentation packages for internal and external stakeholders.

Analyze recurring indirect tax processes to identify manual bottlenecks, designing and implementing low-code solutions via Microsoft Power Platform (Power Automate, Power Apps) to drive efficiency.

Develop, test, and maintain AI-enabled workflows and automated controls for tax data validation, reporting, and compliance routine processes.

Create interactive dashboards and reports using Power BI and Excel to transform raw tax transaction data into clear, actionable business insights.

Support ERP tax configurations and system integrations, participating in user acceptance testing (UAT) for digital tax platform updates.

Deliver high-quality customer service to internal stakeholders (Sales, Credit teams), translating operational tax challenges into practical digital solution requirements.

Stay informed of developments in indirect tax regulations and AI capabilities, proactively identifying how legislative changes impact existing automated workflows and tax technologies.

Project Management & Delivery Support

Support the planning, execution, testing, and implementation of indirect tax technology and automation initiatives.

Collaborate with Tax, Finance, IT, and business stakeholders to gather requirements and translate business needs into practical digital solutions.

Coordinate user acceptance testing (UAT), defect tracking, and validation of automation solutions.

Monitor project milestones, risks and action items to support timely project delivery.

Prepare project documentation, user guides, and status updates for stakeholders.

Collaboration and Continuous Improvement

Develop and maintain documentation for automation solutions, process flows, technical specifications, and standard operating procedures.

Share best practices, reusable automation components, AI use cases, and lessons learned across the tax team.

Provide user training and ongoing support to encourage adoption of automation and AI-enabled solutions.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand business processes, gather requirements, and drive digital transformation initiatives within the tax function.

Foster a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and knowledge sharing across the organization.

Continuously expand technical and tax knowledge through self-learning, formal training, and participation in team knowledge-sharing initiatives.

Support the preparation of presentations, reports, and management updates related to automation initiatives, tax operations, and project progress.

Qualifications & Requirements

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Business Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

2 - 4 years of relevant experience in automation, digital solutions, software development or a related discipline.

Fresh graduates and candidates with internship or project-based experience in Power Platform or RPA are encouraged to apply.

Experience with ERP systems and tax engines (Oracle, Vertex) is preferred.

Demonstrated interest or academic coursework in AI, machine learning or business process automation is an advantage.

Technical Skills

Basic working knowledge of Microsoft Power Platform components: Power Automate, Power Apps, and Power BI.

Familiarity with Microsoft 365 applications including SharePoint and Teams.

Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including data analysis and reporting functions.

Basic knowledge of SQL, data querying, or data analytics tools is an advantage.

Basic understanding of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) concepts, AI-enabled solutions, workflow automation, and low-code/no-code development concepts.

Knowledge of Agile methodologies and their application in delivering digital automation solutions.

Core Competencies & Soft Skills

Strong analytical and critical thinking skills with excellent attention to detail and a structured approach to problem-solving.

Effective written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present technical concepts in a clear and collaborate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Curiosity and a growth mindset, with a strong willingness to learn new technologies, AI capabilities, and digital solutions.

Strong collaboration and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively across Tax, Finance, IT, and other business functions while managing multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.

Proactive in identifying opportunities to improve processes, enhance efficiency, and support digital transformation initiatives.

Demonstrates professionalism, integrity, and sound judgment when handling confidential and sensitive information.

Preferred Certifications

Microsoft Power Platform Fundamentals (PL-900)

Microsoft Power Automate RPA Developer Associate (PL-500)

Professional Scrum Master I / Certified Scrum Master (PSM/CSM)

jobs.description:
Job (Assignment) Title: SOC Analyst II

Function/Department: Security / Information Technology

Reports To: Manager Security Operations and Engineering

POSITION SUMMARY

- The SOC Analyst II is responsible for overseeing cybersecurity by monitoring, detecting, investigating, and responding to security incidents within an organization. And act as an escalation from Tier 1 analyst. This role focuses on incident analysis, threat validation, containment actions, and root cause identification, while supporting continuous improvement of SOC detections, playbooks, and threat intelligence integration.

The Level II analyst acts as a technical escalation point, mentoring junior analysts and collaborating closely with Incident Response, Threat Intelligence, and Security Engineering teams

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Monitor security events and alerts from SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) systems/ SOAR, 7AI Dashboard and other security tools.

- Perform deep-dive analysis of security alerts escalated by Tier 1 to determine legitimacy, scope, and impact

- Conduct log correlation and forensic analysis across SIEM, EDR, network, cloud, and identity platforms

- Analyze and investigate security incidents to determine their impact and root cause.

- Respond to security incidents, coordinate with stakeholders, and escalate as necessary.

- Conduct risk analysis to identify security gaps.

- Develop and implement incident response procedures and playbooks.

- Collaborate with IT and security teams to improve security configurations and defenses.

- Document security incidents, findings, and recommendations for future mitigation.

- Stay updated on the latest cybersecurity threats, trends, and best practices.

- Identify Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) and attack patterns using threat intelligence and MITRE ATT&CK

- Execute containment and remediation actions (e.g., isolate hosts, block indicators, disable accounts)

- Work with our Security Engineering group for any security application and tools within SOC for enhancement or fine tuning.

- Assist in threat hunting and proactive security monitoring.

- Participate in security awareness training and initiatives.

jobs.title: AI Insights & Governance Analyst
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The AI Insights & Governance Analyst will drive visibility and measurable value realization across Vertiv's AI portfolio. This role owns the analytics layer for enterprise AI—tracking use case value, tool adoption, usage and proficiency, and governance compliance—and translates it into executive-ready insight that informs investment and prioritization decisions. The ideal candidate is fluent in the AI landscape and AI lifecycle, strong in analytics and stakeholder communication, but need not be a deep technical/engineering practitioner.

Key Responsibilities

- Track and quantify business value delivered by AI use cases—cost savings, productivity gains, revenue impact—across Vertiv's global processes (SIOP, NPDI, OTO, OTC) and functions.

- Build and maintain centralized dashboards covering: AI use case portfolio, enterprise AI tool adoption, and user engagement/usage trends/proficiency levels.

- Monitor and report KPIs for the Enterprise AI Tool, including adoption, usage frequency, response quality, and business outcomes.

- Analyze enterprise usage of internal and external AI tools and surface optimization opportunities.

- Define and track AI governance metrics: compliance, approved-model usage, and adherence to enterprise AI policies.

- Partner with business, IT, and AI teams to standardize value-measurement frameworks and reporting structures.

- Produce executive-level scorecards, summaries, and insights for the ELT/leadership audience.

- Support intake and prioritization of new AI use cases with analytics on expected value and impact.

- Identify gaps in adoption, training, or tooling and recommend data-driven improvements.

Requirements

- Bachelor’s degree in business Analytics, Information Systems, Data Analytics, or a related field.

- 2–4 years in business analytics, reporting, or data analysis roles, including hands-on work within AI/GenAI initiatives.

- Solid working knowledge of the AI/GenAI landscape, tools, and vendors—able to speak credibly with both business and technical stakeholders without requiring a deep engineering background.

- Strong analytical skills with proven experience in data visualization and reporting tools (Power BI, QuickSight, or equivalent).

- Ability to translate business metrics into structured reporting and insight.

- Experience working across cross-functional teams (business, IT, product).

- Strong communication skills for executive-facing reporting.

Preferred Qualifications

- Direct experience supporting AI/GenAI programs or enterprise AI initiatives.

- Familiarity with the AI lifecycle (use case intake, deployment, governance, monitoring).

- Knowledge of enterprise AI platforms and ecosystems (e.g., AWS AI services, internal AI platforms).

- Experience defining KPIs and performance-measurement frameworks.

- Exposure to data platforms (e.g., Snowflake or similar).

Core Skills

- Business analytics and KPI development

- Data visualization and dashboarding

- AI adoption, usage, and proficiency analysis

- Stakeholder communication and executive reporting

- Governance tracking and compliance awareness

Performance Measures

- Accuracy and completeness of AI value tracking across use cases

- Quality and usability of dashboards and executive reports

jobs.title: Director of Global Category Management for Professional Services
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Director of Global Category Management for Professional Services is responsible for overseeing all aspects of negotiation, acquisition, and management of professional services engagements critical to Vertiv's enterprise operations and transformation agenda. This strategic role encompasses management consulting, IT professional services, HR, legal, finance, marketing and engineering services, staff augmentation including vendor management solutions, outsourced business services, and advisory engagements across all Vertiv regions. This role is essential for optimising Vertiv's professional services supply base — ensuring the organisation secures high-quality, outcome-driven engagements that align with business objectives while adapting procurement strategies to reflect the evolving AI-enabled services landscape. This role requires strong leadership capabilities to drive the execution of global strategies and set regional direction in collaboration with global procurement leadership. Additionally, this role will play a key role in fostering high-performing teams and ensuring alignment between procurement initiatives and overall business goals, making them a pivotal asset in our organisational success.

The ideal candidate will develop and implement category strategies that meet the diverse needs of business partners across the enterprise, while effectively managing a supply base that drives growth, value realisation, and profitability across all Vertiv regions. They must possess extensive experience in professional services procurement within complex, multi-regional environments, demonstrating a proven track record of delivering global category strategies that enhance cost efficiencies, strengthen supplier relationships, and reposition how the organisation contracts services engagements as AI reshapes the market.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Strategic Procurement: Collaborate closely with Vertiv business leaders to identify and source partners for professional services engagements — including management consulting, IT services, HR, legal, finance, marketing and engineering services, staff augmentation, and outsourced business services — ensuring alignment with organisational objectives.

- Partner Compliance: Work with business units to enforce compliance with data protection measures, intellectual property safeguards, and regulations governing professional services engagements across all regions.

- Supplier Programme Management: Oversee the preferred supplier programme for professional services, developing tailored plans for each partner to ensure business continuity, optimal performance, and competitive pricing.

- Cross-Functional Leadership: Lead cross-functional teams in analysing historical spend data, conducting market research, and employing cost modelling techniques to uncover high-value opportunities that drive innovation, operational efficiency, and risk mitigation across the professional services portfolio.

- Cost Modelling: Establish comprehensive rate card benchmarking, total cost of engagement, and outcome-based pricing models for key categories, ensuring alignment with stakeholder needs and procurement strategies.

- Sourcing Strategy Development: Create and implement effective sourcing, negotiation, and contracting strategies — including outcome-based, time-and-materials, and hybrid engagement models — to achieve desired outcomes consistent with global indirect procurement category strategies.

- Strategic Leadership: Formulate and execute a robust procurement strategy for professional services, enhancing operational efficiency and aligning with organisational goals — including repositioning how Vertiv contracts services engagements as AI reshapes the market.

- Supplier Relationship Management: Identify, evaluate, and cultivate strategic partnerships with key professional services firms, ensuring high-quality, reliable, and competitively priced advisory, consulting, and delivery services.

- Cost Efficiency Initiatives: Spearhead cost reduction initiatives and value analysis processes to optimise the total cost of engagement and maximise return on professional services investment.

- Risk Management: Conduct in-depth market analyses and risk assessments — including evaluation of AI-driven service delivery models — to proactively mitigate supply chain disruptions and ensure compliance with industry standards.

- Collaboration: Partner with IT, HR, finance, legal, marketing operations, and business unit leaders to understand project requirements, ensuring seamless alignment on procurement timelines, specifications, and engagement governance.

- Standardisation: Standardise tools, processes, and contracting frameworks for professional services procurement — including statement of work templates, rate card governance, and vendor management system integration.

- Team Development: Mentor and lead a high-performing procurement team, fostering a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and professional growth.

- Performance Measurement: Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to evaluate procurement effectiveness, supplier performance, and engagement outcomes.

- Reporting: Prepare and present comprehensive reports to senior management on procurement performance, trends, and strategic insights to inform decision-making.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education:

- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field.

- Master's degree or relevant professional certifications (e.g., CPSM, CIPS, MCIPS) preferred.

Experience:

- Minimum of 10 years in procurement or supply chain management, with at least 5 years in a leadership role focused on professional services procurement within a complex, multi-regional environment.

- Proven track record in developing and executing global category strategies that drive cost efficiencies and supplier performance across professional services categories.

- Deep understanding of professional services engagement models, rate card structures, outcome-based contracting, and the evolving impact of AI on services delivery.

- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and manage multiple priorities effectively.

- Track record of establishing and monitoring key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure procurement effectiveness and drive results.

ANTICIPATED BUSINESS TRAVEL: ~30%

jobs.title: Technical Sales Manager – Power
jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced Technical Sales Manager to support the growth of our Power business, with a particular focus on electrical power distribution solutions for data centre and mission-critical applications.

This role sits at the intersection of technical expertise and commercial development. You will work alongside our Sales teams and customers to develop power solutions covering the electrical infrastructure from grid connection and medium-voltage distribution through to low-voltage systems and ultimately the critical load.

The portfolio includes medium-voltage and low-voltage switchgear, busbar systems, UPS, electrical protection and automation, and prefabricated power solutions.

You will act as a technical partner to customers, helping them understand how different technologies can be brought together to create reliable, resilient and scalable power infrastructure.

We are particularly interested in candidates who understand complex electrical power distribution and can combine that knowledge with a commercial, customer-focused approach. Experience within data centres would be highly relevant, although we also welcome candidates from industries such as utilities, power generation, oil & gas, chemicals and other environments with large-scale electrical distribution infrastructure.
Key Responsibilities

- Work alongside Sales teams to identify and develop opportunities across the electrical power distribution portfolio.

- Engage directly with customers to understand their power requirements, technical challenges and future infrastructure needs.

- Develop technically and commercially appropriate solutions using technologies including MV and LV switchgear, busbar, UPS, protection and automation systems and prefabricated power solutions.

- Provide technical guidance throughout the sales process, from initial customer discussions through specification, proposal and solution development.

- Review customer specifications, RFQs and tender requirements and translate these into appropriate technical solutions.

- Prepare and deliver technical presentations, proposals and customer workshops.

- Work closely with engineering, product and manufacturing teams to ensure proposed solutions are technically viable and aligned with Vertiv capabilities.

- Act as a technical link between regional Sales teams and the Power Line of Business.

- Maintain an understanding of developments across the power distribution market, including new technologies, competitor solutions and changing customer requirements.

- Support opportunity and pipeline management through accurate CRM information.

Qualifications & Experience

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical discipline.

- Ideally 10+ years' experience within electrical power distribution, technical sales, sales engineering, application engineering or solution development.

- Strong understanding of medium- and low-voltage electrical distribution systems .

- Experience with technologies such as switchgear, busbar/busway, UPS, electrical protection, power automation or related power distribution equipment .

- Demonstrable experience developing or supporting complex electrical infrastructure solutions.

- Strong commercial awareness with the ability to translate technical requirements into customer-focused solutions.

- Experience working with customers, consultants, contractors or engineering organisations.

- Data centre or mission-critical infrastructure experience is highly desirable, although relevant industrial power experience is equally valuable.

- Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to engage technical and commercial stakeholders.

- Willingness to travel across the region as required.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager Mergers and Acquisitions Integration
jobs.description:
Our Integration Management Office is the central hub that brings newly acquired businesses into Vertiv and turns our deal thesis into realized value. We are hiring a Senior Manager, Integration, to join the IMO and lead the integration of assigned acquisitions end to end, operating within our established integration governance, playbook, and toolset.

What you will own

Reporting to the Vice President, Global M&A Integration, you will serve as the integration lead for assigned the value-creation case from pre-close planning through Day 1 and the value-capture period that follows. You will drive the integration plan across functional workstreams, hold the program to the synergy and milestone commitments defined in diligence, and partner with acquired-company leadership to implement our integration playbook while protecting the talent, customers, and culture that made the business worth acquiring.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to

- Lead integrations end to end:  Own the integration roadmap for assigned deals, from diligence handoff and Day 1 readiness through the value-capture period, anchored to the value-creation thesis approved at deal approval.

- Run the integration within the IMO model:  Operate inside the IMO established governance, charters, tools, and templates; manage cross-functional workstreams across Finance, HR, IT, Operations, Commercial, Legal, and Supply Chain; and keep steering committees informed with a disciplined reporting cadence.

- Deliver measurable value capture:  Translate the deal model into tracked synergy and improvement commitments across safety, quality, delivery, and cost; establish the metrics, dashboards, and review rhythm that hold the integration accountable to the case.

- Deploy operational efficiency and integration playbook into acquired businesses:  Partner with acquired leadership to introduce lean and Lean Six Sigma processes, Value Stream Mapping, daily management, and policy deployment, establishing visual management so teams have immediate feedback on performance.

- Lead through influence:  Build trust quickly across newly acquired leadership teams, corporate functions, and IMO workstream leads, driving alignment without direct reporting authority.

- Protect what we acquired:  Steward culture, key talent, and customer relationships through the transition, recognizing that retaining the acquired team strengths is as critical to the thesis as capturing synergies.

- Strengthen the IMO playbook:  Capture lessons learned, refine integration tools and templates, and contribute to raising the consistency, maturity, and repeatability of integration across the Vertiv deal pipeline.

The essential requirements of the job include

- Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, finance, or a related field; MBA preferred.

- Eight or more years of progressive experience in M&A integration, corporate development, operations, program management, or management consulting, including direct experience leading or co-leading post-merger and post-acquisition integration.

- Demonstrated success delivering complex, cross-functional programs on time and on budget while leading through influence in a matrixed, global organization.

- Strong financial and analytical fluency, able to connect an integration plan to a deal model, synergy targets, and P&L outcomes.

- Working knowledge of lean and continuous-improvement methodologies such as Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, or an equivalent operating system.

- Excellent communication and change-leadership skills, credible with both frontline teams and senior executives.

- Willingness to travel 40 to 60 percent, including internationally.

It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in

- Operating within an established IMO or enterprise PMO across multiple, concurrent integrations.

- Critical infrastructure, power, thermal or cooling, electrical equipment, industrial technology, or data center end markets.

- Carve-out, cross-border, or bolt-on integration at scale across multiple acquisitions.

- A formal operating-system or continuous improvement practitioner or certification background, for example a Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent.

We are hiring a Senior Manager, Integration, to join the IMO and lead the integration of assigned acquisitions end to end, operating within our established integration governance, playbook, and toolset.
