jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Procurement Strategic Operations & Governance Leader is responsible for driving the effective operation, governance, and strategic execution of the Global Procurement organisation.

The role acts as a strategic partner to Procurement leadership, ensuring that the organisation operates through a clear and effective operating model, robust governance, consistent processes, and disciplined execution of strategic priorities.

The Leader owns the Procurement leadership operating cadence and ensures that strategic decisions, actions, and commitments are translated into execution and followed through to closure.

The successful candidate will be a highly credible Procurement professional who can operate comfortably between strategic leadership and detailed execution. They will be capable of understanding complex business issues, simplifying them for senior leadership, and creating the governance and accountability required to deliver results.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Procurement Strategic Operations:

- Partner with Procurement leadership to translate strategic priorities into executable plans

- Establish and manage the Procurement strategic operating rhythm

- Coordinate cross-functional and regional activities required to execute Procurement priorities

- Identify risks, dependencies, and execution gaps and ensure appropriate escalation

-
Provide strategic support on emerging priorities and ad-hoc leadership requirements

Executive Leadership & Procurement Cadence:

Own the end-to-end management of Procurement's executive cadence, including:

- Procurement QBRs

- MORs and operational reviews

- Procurement Townhalls

- Board and Executive Leadership presentations

- Growth Days

- CPO and Procurement Leadership meetings

-
Other strategic Procurement presentations and forums

Responsibilities include:

- Agenda development and planning

- Content coordination across Procurement

- Executive storyline development

- Data and message alignment

- Preparation and quality control of materials

- Action tracking and follow-up

- Driving actions through to closure

- Maintaining visibility of outstanding commitments and escalations

Procurement Operating Model

Own the ongoing development and governance of the Procurement operating model.

Responsibilities include:

- Define and maintain the Procurement process and governance framework

- Establish clear ownership for Procurement policies and processes

- Identify and close gaps in the existing operating model

- Develop new policies, processes, standards, and governance mechanisms where required

- Establish formal review and refresh cycles

- Ensure processes remain aligned with organisational strategy and business requirements

-
Drive standardisation across regions whilst recognising appropriate local requirements

Policy & Process Governance

- Maintain a central register of Procurement policies and processes

- Define process owners and accountability

- Monitor review cycles and completion

- Identify duplication, gaps, and opportunities for simplification

-
Drive continuous improvement of the Procurement operating framework

Procurement Transformation Governance

- Establish governance for strategic initiatives

- Track milestones, dependencies, risks, and actions

- Ensure transformation initiatives remain aligned to CPO priorities

- Provide leadership reporting on transformation progress

Procurement Knowledge Management

Own the governance of Procurement's digital knowledge environment, including the Procurement Hub and SharePoint.

Responsibilities include:

- Content governance.

- Structure and accessibility

- Document ownership

- Version control

- Standard templates and resources

- Ensuring critical Procurement information remains current

-
Establishing clear ownership for ongoing maintenance

Leadership Team Support & Strategic Projects

- Act as a trusted execution partner to the Procurement Leadership Team within the Corporate Strategy Function

- Support strategic organisational initiatives

- Coordinate complex cross-functional requests

- Lead special projects on behalf of Procurement leadership

- Respond to emerging and ad-hoc business requirement

- Provide structured problem solving and recommendations to leadership

Key Interfaces

- Chief Procurement Officer

- Procurement Leadership Team

- Regional Procurement Leaders

- Category and Business Unit Leaders

- Finance

- Operations

- Supply Chain

- Engineering

- IT / Digital

- HR

- Legal

- Executive Leadership

- Corporate Strategy

Key Success Measures

- Effectiveness and timeliness of Procurement leadership cadence

- Closure rate of leadership actions and commitments

- Operating model maturity

- Policy and process governance compliance

- Strategic initiative execution

- Reduction in process and governance gaps

- Stakeholder satisfaction

- Effectiveness of Procurement communications and executive reporting

- Adoption of standard Procurement processes

QUALIFICATIONS

Required Capabilities

- Industry experience: 8+ years' experience in Strategy, Programme and portfolio management, PMO management etc

- Procurement governance and operating model design : experience designing corporate governance frameworks and scalable operating models that align with long-term strategy.

- Strategic thinking and execution: Ability to think long-term and plan for future business needs.

- Roadmap Development: Proven capability to translate high-level strategy into actionable, tactical execution plans.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

The Product Line Project Manager, Global Procurement is the single point of contact for Procurement on assigned projects (NPDI, ETO, SFA, VAVE, sustaining). This is an individual contributor role responsible for establishing a resilient, cost‑effective, and scalable supply chain for new products by driving early supplier engagement, sourcing strategy execution, and procurement readiness throughout the NPDI phase‑gate process.

Responsibilities:

Project Ownership and Cross-Functional Alignment

- Serve as the primary Procurement representative for assigned projects from early concept through production readiness.

- Ensure procurement deliverables are planned, tracked, and executed in alignment with NPDI phase-gate requirements.

- Represent Procurement at NPDI gate reviews, providing clear visibility into sourcing maturity, gaps, and mitigations.

- Track and report key metrics such as cost, lead time, supplier performance, and launch readiness.

- Partner closely with Engineering, Program Management, Commodity Management, Quality, and Operations teams to ensure sourcing strategies support overall project objectives.

- Act as the primary escalation point for procurement related risks impacting cost, schedule, or supply resilience.

Early Supplier Engagement and Sourcing Strategy

- Engage proactively with Engineering to understand component requirements early in the design process.

- Engage suppliers early to assess technical capability, capacity, cost drivers, and lead time expectations.

- Send early RFQs/RFPs ahead of design release and drive competitive bidding to achieve cost targets.

- Facilitate collaboration between Engineering and suppliers to improve design for manufacturability, cost efficiency, and supply flexibility.

- Establish strong supplier partnerships to drive innovation, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement.

- Ensure sourcing approaches align with established commodity strategies and preferred supplier frameworks.

Cost, Risk, and Supply Chain Readiness

- Support prototype, pilot, and pre-production builds, ensuring on-time availability of materials and services.

- Ensure sourcing aligns with NPDI resilience expectations (multi‑source, regional manufacturing, avoidance of single‑point failures).

- Use standardized BOM cost and risk tracking tools to maintain consistency and transparency.

- Promote reuse of existing, qualified components and architectures where feasible to improve cost, availability, and time‑to‑market.

- Drive sourcing maturity and readiness prior to product release to minimize disruption during ramp up and production.

Qualifications:

An ideal candidate will bring…

- Experience in Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, or Supply Chain, supporting new product or engineering driven programs.

- Experience working closely with Engineering teams during early product development.

- Strong communication skills with the ability to influence across functions without direct authority.

- Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a matrixed, cross functional environment.

- Experience supporting global supply chains and multiple manufacturing regions.

- Familiarity with phase-gate or structured product development processes.

Education:

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Mechanical, Industrial, Electrical, Electronic), Supply Chain Operations and/or Business is preferred.

Physical Requirements:

- No Special Physical Requirements

Environmental Demands:

- No Specific Environmental Demands

Travel Time Required:

- Ability to work overtime and travel (domestically and internationally) up to 15% is required.

- Ability to work as per Project priorities and take after hours calls as necessary.

- Strong commercial negotiation, contract management, analytical and stakeholder-management skills.

- Ability to read and interpret drawings specifications, drawings, data sheets, test requirements and supplier technical proposals.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and ERP/procurement systems; experience with Power BI or similar analytics tools is preferred.

- Fluent business English and willingness to travel regionally as required.

Key Performance Indicators

- Supplier on-time delivery and lead-time improvement

- Supplier quality and corrective-action closure

- Localization and alternate-source implementation

- Contract coverage and sourcing compliance

- Inventory and working-capital improvement

- Supplier risk reduction and continuity readiness

- Project sourcing milestones and stakeholder satisfaction

- ESG and supplier-compliance performance

Preferred Industry Exposure
Candidates with sourcing or engineering exposure in the following sectors will be preferred:

- UPS/ DC and critical power systems

- Data centers and telecom power

- Industrial energy storage

- Power generation and utilities

The ideal candidate is a technically credible and commercially strong sourcing professional who can translate business demand into a clear commodity strategy, create competitive supplier options and deliver measurable improvements in cost, quality, delivery and supply resilience. jobs.title: SIOP Strategic Planning Analyst
jobs.description:
Purpose of the Role

The Strategic Planning Analyst is a newly created role within the EMEA SI&OP organization, designed to close a critical gap in long-term planning and scenario analysis. This role focuses on the strategic horizon of supply planning - translating market signals, Big Bets, and pipeline opportunities into long-term workload plans, investment business cases, and multi-plant allocation strategies.

Key Responsibilities

- Collect and prepare data for the Strategic planning process, collecting demand signals and converting them into long-term workload projections.

- Develop strategic workload allocation plans across multiple EMEA plants, IS projects, ICO business, and NPDI initiatives.

- Build investment business cases in collaboration with AME, Procurement, and Finance to support capacity expansion or reallocation decisions.

- Link SI&OP to Procurement by providing strategic volume outlooks that drive long-term purchasing strategies and supplier development.

- Conduct scenario planning and what-if analyses to evaluate the impact of demand shifts, capacity constraints, or new product introductions on the regional supply network.

- Participate in Large/Top Projects workstreams, ensuring strategic supply considerations are embedded in project planning from inception.

- Maintain a weekly cadence with Sales Leadership, AME, and Procurement to capture evolving strategic inputs and align long-term plans.

- Support Six Sigma projects (Green Belt level) focused on improving strategic planning accuracy and process maturity.

- Contribute to Kinaxis implementation efforts, particularly in configuring strategic/long-range planning modules.

- Prepare executive-level reports and presentations summarizing strategic supply outlook, risks, and investment recommendations for SI&OP governance forums.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, or related field.

- 3–5 years of experience in supply chain planning, strategic planning, or operations analysis, preferably in a manufacturing environment.

- Strong analytical and modeling skills; experience with scenario planning and what-if analysis.

- Familiarity with S&OP/SI&OP processes and workload-capacity frameworks.

- Experience with APS/ERP systems (Kinaxis experience is a plus).

- Six Sigma Green Belt certification or willingness to obtain one.

- Excellent communication skills with the ability to present to senior leadership.

- Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.
